<!-- maintheorem-1: body_md -->
\label{mainthm:Niceness properties}
    Let $n \geq 2$ be an integer. The logarithmic generalised Kummer construction equips a compactification $\mathcal{K}_{2n}^\circ\hookrightarrow \mathcal{K}_{2n}$ of the generalised Kummer locus with a universal family 
     $$\pi_{2n} \colon \mathcal U_{2n} \longrightarrow \mathcal K_{2n}$$
     of logarithmic IHS varieties. Moreover, both $\mathcal{K}_{2n}$ and $\mathcal{U}_{2n}$ are proper \textit{logarithmic Deligne--Mumford (DM) stacks}, and thus admit a logarithmic \'etale cover by schemes with logarithmic structure.
<!-- end maintheorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:promise}
    Every time we introduce a logarithmic space or logarithmic DM stack $\mathcal{X}$ which is not a DM stack with logarithmic structure, we will also specify an associated tropical object $\mathpzc{X}$.\footnote{We reserve the latter font for stacks on the tropical site (i.e. the face site of \cite{ModStckTropCurve}).} A logarithmic space specifies an equivalence class of schemes with logarithmic structure. Elements of the equivalence class are called logarithmic alterations of $\mathcal{X}$. The dual intersection complex of each logarithmic alteration of $\mathcal{X}$ admits a canonical map to the link of a cone complex subdividing $\mathpzc{X}$. This map is often an isomorphism. Figure \ref{fig:firstTropAv} illustrates the discussion of Section \ref{sec:logspaces}, which explains how logarithmic alterations can be read--off from a combinatorial choice: a cone complex structure on the attendant tropical gadget.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- maintheorem-2: body_md -->
\label{Thm:maintrop}
Let $n\geq 2$. The tropical generalised Kummer construction  equips $\mathpzc{K}_{2n}$ with a universal family 
$$\mathpzc{U}_{2n}\rightarrow \mathpzc{K}_{2n}$$ of integral affine manifolds with singularities. The topological realisation of each fibre is homeomorphic to either $\mathbb{CP}^n$, an $n$-simplex, or a point. There is a commutative square (in the category of CFG over the category of logarithmic schemes) with strict horizontal maps $$\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal{U}_{2n} \arrow[r,"\hat{\varpi}"] \arrow[d]
  & a^{\ast}  \mathpzc{U}_{2n} \arrow[d] \\
\mathcal K_{2n} \arrow[r, "\varpi"]
  & a^{\ast} \mathpzc{K}_{2n}.
\end{tikzcd}
$$
<!-- end maintheorem-2 -->
<!-- maintheorem-3: body_md -->
\label{mainthm:ReadOffModel}
    Let $n\geq 2$. Consider any of the (infinitely many) choices, indexed by $\Lambda$, of diagrams of stacks upon the tropical site, 
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd} 
    \mathpzc{U}_{2n}^\Lambda \arrow[r] \arrow[d,"p"]
  & \mathpzc{U}_{2n} \arrow[d] \\
\mathpzc K_{2n}^\Lambda \arrow[r]
  & \mathpzc{K}_{2n}.
\end{tikzcd}$$
    where the horizontal maps are tropical alterations (i.e. compositions of subdivisions and changes of lattice), and $p$ is a saturated morphism of cone stacks. The base change of the diagram of Theorem~\ref{Thm:maintrop} yields a vertical, saturated, and logarithmically smooth morphism 
    $$\mathcal{U}_{2n}^\Lambda = \mathcal{U}_{2n}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{U}_{2n}}a^\ast \mathpzc{U}^\Lambda_{2n}\rightarrow \mathcal{K}_{2n}^\Lambda = \mathcal{K}_{2n}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{K}_{2n}} a^\ast \mathpzc{K}^\Lambda_{2n}$$
    in the category of DM stacks with logarithmic structure. Moreover, the open immersion $\mathcal{K}_{2n}^\circ \hookrightarrow \mathcal{K}_{2n}^\Lambda$ is a toroidal compactification.
<!-- end maintheorem-3 -->
<!-- maintheorem-4: body_md -->
\label{mainthm:1param} Let $n\geq 1$ be any positive integer.
    The dual intersection complex of central fibre to the one-parameter degeneration $$\pi \colon \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(A) \rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A) \rightarrow \Delta$$
    is canonically the polyhedral complex $B_\Lambda$.
<!-- end maintheorem-4 -->
<!-- maintheorem-5: body_md -->
\label{mainthm:Explicit}
    Let $n\geq 1$ be any positive integer. Choosing $\Lambda$ such that $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(A)\rightarrow \Delta$$ is semistable (and in particular saturated), the irreducible components of the central fibre admit the following explicit description: 
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item \textbf{(Scheme-theoretic, interior only.)} The underlying DM stack of the interior of each irreducible component of the central fibre is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}}(A^{\circ})$ where the tuple $\textbf{n}=(n_1,...,n_k)$ is the collision type associated to this irreducible component.
        \item \textbf{(Logarithmic category, whole irreducible component.)} The underlying DM stack of each irreducible component of the central fibre is a logarithmic alteration of $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ where the tuple $\textbf{n}= (n_1,...,n_k)$ is the associated collision type. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end maintheorem-5 -->
<!-- mainconjecture-1: body_md -->
\label{Conj}
    Let $\operatorname{M}_{\operatorname{K3}}^{\log}$ denote the moduli stack of polarised descending logarithmic IHS surfaces, and let $\operatorname{M}_{\operatorname{tor}}$ denote the space obtained by log \'etale sheafifying the functor of points of any toroidal compactification of the moduli of polarised K3 surfaces. There is a commutative square 
    $$                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{M}_{K3}^{\log} \arrow[r, "\pi"] \arrow[d] & \operatorname{M}_{\operatorname{tor}} \arrow[d] \\
a^\ast \operatorname{M}_{K3}^{\operatorname{trop}} \arrow[r,"\pi^{\operatorname{trop}}"]   & a^\ast \Omega^{\operatorname{trop}}                   
\end{tikzcd}$$
where $\pi$ is a categorical moduli space for the category of descending logarithmic spaces; $\operatorname{M}_{K3}^{\operatorname{trop}}$ is an (as yet undefined) moduli space of integral affine manifolds with singularities; and $\Omega^{\operatorname{trop}}$ is an (as of yet undefined) appropriate tropical period domain parallel to the constructions of \cite{ChanEtAlTropSymm}.
<!-- end mainconjecture-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
The \textit{underlying topological space} $|\sigma|$ of a cone $\sigma\subset \mathbb{Z}^n$ is the subset $\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}\otimes \sigma$ of $\mathbb{R}^n$ equipped with the subspace topology from $\mathbb{R}^n$. The underlying topological space of a cone complex $\Sigma$, where we express $\Sigma$ as the colimit over a diagram $$J\rightarrow \mathsf{RPCC}$$ of rational polyhedral cones, is the colimit over the induced diagram in the category of topological spaces.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A \textit{subdivision} of a rational polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is a morphism of sheaves which arises from a subdivision of $\sigma$ in the category of fans \cite{Fulton+2016}. A subdivision of a sheaf $\mathpzc{F}$ on \textbf{RPC} is a morphism of sheaves $$\mathcal{F}_\Sigma \rightarrow \mathpzc{F}$$ represented by subdivisions of rational polyhedral cones. A \textit{tropical alteration} of a rational polyhedral cone $\sigma$ is a monomorphism $\Sigma \rightarrow \sigma$ in the category RPCC which induces an isomorphism on underlying topological spaces. A morphism of sheaves on \textbf{RPC} is said to be a tropical alteration if it is represented by tropical alterations of rational polyhedral cones. A tropical model of a sheaf $\mathpzc{F}$ is a tropical alteration with domain a cone complex. The \textit{underlying topological space} $|\mathpzc{F}|$ of a sheaf $\mathpzc{F}$ of sets on \textbf{RPC} which admits a tropical model is the underlying topological space of any tropical model.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
\label{defn:Link}
    Let $\pi \colon \Lambda \rightarrow \rho$ be an exact morphism of cone complexes, inducing a morphism of topological realisations $$\pi_\mathbb{R}\colon |\Lambda| \rightarrow |\rho|.$$ The \textit{link} of $\pi$ is the topological space $\pi_\mathbb{R}^{-1}(1)$. Let $\mathpzc{F}$ be a sheaf on $\textbf{RPC}_\rho$ which admits a tropical model $\Lambda\rightarrow \mathpzc{F}$ exact over $\rho$. The \textit{link of $\mathpzc{F}$} is the link of any such tropical model.\footnote{This is well defined because any two tropical models admit a common alteration (their fibre product over $\mathpzc{F}$), and tropical alterations induce identifications of topological realisations.}
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
An \textit{Artin cone} is a stack with logarithmic structure obtained by taking the global quotient stack of an affine toric variety with toric logarithmic structure by its dense torus. An alteration of an Artin cone $a^\ast \sigma$ is a morphism $a^\ast \Sigma \rightarrow a^\ast \sigma$ induced by a tropical alteration $\Sigma\rightarrow \sigma$ of $\sigma$.
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
A Noetherian logarithmic scheme is said to be atomic if, when stratified by the isomorphism type of the stalk $(M_X/\mathcal{O}_X^\times)_p$, it has a unique stratum which is closed and connected, and the restriction of the sheaf $M_X/\mathcal{O}_X^\times$ to this stratum is the constant sheaf.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Through its functor of points, a cone complex \cite[Section 2.6]{abramovich2015skeletons}, cone stack \cite[Section 2]{ModStckTropCurve}, tropical abelian variety in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:TropicalAV}, or piecewise linear space \cite[Section 1]{LogQuot} can be upgraded to a stack on the category of logarithmic schemes. Only the first two examples give rise to sheaves which are Artin stacks equipped with logarithmic structure.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
For $X$ a Noetherian logarithmic scheme (over the complex numbers) there is a cone stack $\mathsf{Trop}(X)$ (i.e. a stack on \textbf{RPC} satisfying representability properties described in \cite{ModStckTropCurve}) and a strict morphism
    $${X}\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_X := a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(X)$$ which is initial among strict maps from $X$ to an Artin fan with faithful monodromy. We call $\mathcal{A}_X$ \textit{the} Artin fan of $X$. Consider any morphism of Noetherian logarithmic schemes $f\colon X\rightarrow Y$. There is an initial Artin fan $\mathcal{A}_{X/Y}$ which fits into a commutative square with strict vertical arrows of the following shape:
    $$\begin{tikzcd}
X \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & Y \arrow[d] \\
\mathcal{A}_{X/Y} \arrow[r] & \mathcal{A}_Y
\end{tikzcd}.$$
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
An effective Cartier divisor on a smooth scheme $\underline{X}$ specifies a map from $\underline{X}$ to $[\mathbb{A}^1/\mathbb{G}_m]$. Thus, a strict normal crossing pair $(X,D=\sum_iD_i)$ such that every intersect of $D_i$ is connected, together with an ordering on the $D_i$ is the same data as a morphism $$\varpi\colon X\rightarrow [\mathbb{A}^n/\mathbb{G}_m^n] = a^\ast \Sigma.$$ Note $\mathsf{Trop}(X)\subset \Sigma$ is a sub-cone complex; potentially a proper sub-cone complex as $\varpi$ need not hit the closed point of $a^\ast \Sigma$.
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- example-2: body_md -->
Consider a strict normal crossing degeneration: a map $\pi\colon X \rightarrow \mathbb{A}^1$ such that the central fibre is a strict normal crossing divisor $\pi^{-1}(0) = \sum_iD_i$. Since the Artin fan of $\mathbb{A}^1$ is a cone, \cite[Lemma A.21]{herr2026loggeometryliftingrational} ensures that the Artin fan construction is functorial in this case. We thus obtain a commutative square,
    $$
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
\begin{tikzcd}
X \arrow[d] \arrow[r]              & \mathbb{A}^1 \arrow[d] \\
a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(X) \arrow[r] & a^\ast \rho = a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(\mathbb{A}^1).          
\end{tikzcd}
    $$
    Assuming each logarithmic stratum is connected, the underlying topological space of the dual intersection complex of $\pi^{-1}(0)$ can be obtained from the map $\mathsf{Trop}(X)\rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ as the preimage of $1$ under the map $\mathsf{Trop}(X)\otimes\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$. Thus the dual intersection complex is a choice of polyhedral structure upon the link.
<!-- end example-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
In the sequel we often consider logarithmic schemes over some atomic base $S$ with tropicalisation a cone $\kappa$ (i.e. with Artin fan $S\rightarrow a^\ast \kappa$). We are often led to study sheaves on the comma site $\textbf{RPC}_\kappa$ whose objects are morphisms of cone complexes $\sigma\rightarrow \kappa$.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
\label{defn:RayFromDVR}
    The \textit{tropicalisation of $f$} is the unique morphism $$f^\text{trop}\colon \mathbb{N}\rightarrow \Sigma$$ such that $a^\ast f^\text{trop}$ induces the map of the previous paragraph.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
\label{defn:logsmoothold}
    A morphism $f\colon X\rightarrow Y$ of Noetherian logarithmic schemes is said to be \textit{logarithmic \'etale} (resp. \textit{smooth, flat}) if the morphism $$X\rightarrow {\mathcal{A}_{X/Y}}\times_{\mathcal{A}_Y} Y$$ is \'etale (resp. smooth, flat) as a morphism of stacks.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
\label{defn:logAlt}
    A \textit{logarithmic alteration} of a Noetherian DM stack with logarithmic structure $X$ is a morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure $X'\rightarrow X$ which, strict \'etale locally upon $X$, is the base change of an alteration of Artin cones.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
The \textit{logarithmic \'etale site} is the site structure on the category of logarithmic schemes whose covers are generated by strict \'etale covers (inherited from conventional algebraic geometry) and logarithmic alterations. A morphism of sheaves on \textbf{LogSch} is called a logarithmic \'etale cover if it is represented by logarithmic \'etale covers on the category of logarithmic schemes.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
\label{defn:logalgspaces}
    \textit{Logarithmic spaces} are sheaves of sets on \textbf{LogSch} which admit a logarithmic \'etale cover by a scheme with logarithmic structure. A \textit{logarithmic DM stack} is a CFG over \textbf{LogSch} with diagonal representable by logarithmic spaces, and which admits a logarithmic \'etale cover by a scheme with logarithmic structure.
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- example-3: body_md -->
The stack quotient of $\mathbb{A}^1$ (equipped with its toric logarithmic structure) by $\mu_2$ acting via the dense torus of $\mathbb{A}^1$ is a logarithmic space, even though it is obtained by equipping a Deligne--Mumford stack with non-trivial stabiliser with a logarithmic structure. A logarithmic alteration of a logarithmic space $X$ is a morphism in the category of logarithmic spaces $X'\rightarrow X$ represented by logarithmic alterations on the category of logarithmic schemes.
<!-- end example-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
We expect that, in order to generalise the results of this paper to compactify other moduli of IHS varieties, it will be convenient to restrict attention to only those logarithmic spaces whose functor of points satisfies logarithmic \'etale descent. These structures appear as descending logarithmic spaces studied in \cite[Section 4]{logcoh}.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
A \textit{sheafy DM stack with logarithmic structure} is a DM stack with logarithmic structure having the property that, when considered as a CFG over the logarithmic \'etale site, it is a category fibred in setoids (i.e. stabilisers are trivial).
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
\label{defn:loclogsmooth}
    We say that a morphism of logarithmic spaces $X\rightarrow S$ is \textit{locally logarithmically smooth} if, possibly after replacing $S$ by a strict \'etale cover, there exist proper models $S'\rightarrow S$ and $X'\rightarrow X\times_S S'$ such that the induced morphism $X'\rightarrow S'$ is logarithmically smooth in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:logsmoothold}.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
Any morphism of schemes with log structure which is logarithmically smooth is locally logarithmically smooth. The converse is not true, see \cite[Example IV.4.3.4]{OgusBook2018} (or \cite[Example 2.6]{hu2025grothendiecktopologieslogarithmicmodifications} for an exposition). Local logarithmic smoothness is a natural generalisation of logarithmic smoothness to morphisms of descending logarithmic spaces (motivated in Section \ref{sec:outlook}).
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
The author is not aware of an example of a locally logarithmically smooth morphism between static schemes (in the sense of \cite[Definition 2.2.3]{logcoh}) with logarithmic structure where both source and target are static, and which is not logarithmically smooth.
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
We say that a (polarised) saturated, vertical, and logarithmically smooth morphism $Y\rightarrow \Delta_0$ is \textit{(polarised) smoothable} if, possibly after replacing $Y$ and $\Delta_0$ by logarithmic alterations, it coincides (as a polarised logarithmic scheme) with the central fibre to a projective, vertical, logarithmically smooth, and saturated morphism $X\rightarrow \Delta$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
\label{defn:KNSpace}
    Let $Y$ be a scheme with logarithmic structure of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, and write $Y^{an}$ for the associated logarithmic analytic space. The \textit{topological Kato--Nakayama} space $|\operatorname{KN}(Y)|$ is obtained by equipping the set
$$
|\operatorname{KN}(Y)| := \bigl\{\,(x,h) \;\big|\; x \in Y^{an},\ h \colon M_{Y,x}^{\mathrm{gp}} \to S^{1} \text{ group hom with } h(u) = u(x)/|u(x)| \text{ for all } u \in \mathcal{O}_{Y,x}^{*} \bigr\},
$$
with the coarsest topology satisfying the following hypotheses.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin =*]
    \item The projection $\tau \colon |\operatorname{KN}(Y)| \to Y^{an}$, $(x,h) \mapsto x$, is continuous.
    \item For every open $U \subset Y^{an}$ and every section $m \in \Gamma(U, M_Y^{\mathrm{gp}})$, the evaluation map
    $$
    \tau^{-1}(U) \longrightarrow S^{1}, \qquad (x,h) \longmapsto h(m_x),
    $$
    is continuous.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
The (kummer log \'etale) Kato--Nakayama space $\mathsf{KN}(Y)$ associated to $Y$ is a ringed space obtained by equipping $|\operatorname{KN}(Y)|$ with the sheaf of rings $\mathcal{O}_{Y_{\text{k\'et}}}^\text{KN}$ described in \cite[3.2]{IllusieKatoNakayama2005}.
    Following \cite[3.1]{IllusieKatoNakayama2005}, there is a morphism of topoi,
    $$\tau \colon \operatorname{KN}(Y)\rightarrow Y^{an}_{\text{k\'et}}.$$
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:Kummeret}
    The original definition of the Kato--Nakayama space \cite[Section 1]{KatoNakayama1999}, which is consistent with the use throughout \cite{KatoUsui2009}, is equipped with a different (not kummer \'etale) sheaf of rings. The underlying topological space is the same in both versions, and they differ only in their sheaf of functions. In this paper all Kato--Nakayama spaces are the Kummer logarithmic \'etale version.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
Even the topological Kato--Nakayama space of $Y$ is not invariant under non-kummer logarithmic alterations of $Y$. Instead Proposition~\ref{prop:HomotopyGroups} will show that the homotopy type of the Kato--Nakayama space is well defined.
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- lemdefn-1: body_md -->
\label{lemdefn:KNSpace}
    Let $X$ be a separated sheafy DM stack with locally free logarithmic structure of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$, and choose a groupoid presentation
    $$
        s,t\colon R = U\times_X U \rightrightarrows U
    $$
    for $X$, where $U$ and $R$ are schemes with logarithmic structure, and $s,t$ are strict \'etale.\footnote{Note this is the same data as a strict \'etale cover $U\rightarrow X$ by schemes with logarithmic structure, which exists by hypothesis.}
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item The induced morphism in the category of topological spaces $$(s^{\operatorname{KN}},t^{\operatorname{KN}})\colon |\operatorname{KN}(R)|\rightarrow |\operatorname{KN}(U)| \times |{\operatorname{KN}}(U)|$$ is an embedding. Moreover the natural map $q\colon \operatorname{KN}(U) \rightarrow \operatorname{KN}(U)/\operatorname{KN}(R)$ in the category of topological spaces admits local sections. Thus by \cite[Proposition 7.9]{noohi2005foundationstopologicalstacksi} the topological stack quotient $[|\operatorname{KN}(U)|/|\operatorname{KN}(R)|]$ is representable by a topological space which we denote $|{\operatorname{KN}}(X)|$. 
        \item The homeomorphism type of $|{\operatorname{KN}}(X)|$ does not depend on the choice of groupoid presentation.
    \end{enumerate}
    The \textit{Kato--Nakayama} space of $X$, denoted ${\operatorname{KN}}(X)$, is the ringed space obtained by equipping $|{\operatorname{KN}}(X)|$ with the sheaf of rings descended from $\mathcal{O}_{U_{k\acute{e}t}}^{\operatorname{KN}}$.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *, start = 3]
        \item The isomorphism type of ${\operatorname{KN}}(X)$ is independent of the choice of groupoid presentation, and there is a canonical morphism of ringed spaces $$\tau\colon \operatorname{KN}(X)\rightarrow X^{an}.$$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemdefn-1 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
In the logarithmic category, sheafy DM stacks with logarithmic structure behave like non-stacky objects. Lemma/Definition~\ref{lemdefn:KNSpace} captures this fact because their Kato--Nakayama space is naturally a topological space not a topological stack. We will discover that extending the analysis of Kato--Nakayama spaces to sheafy DM stacks with logarithmic structure consequently does not introduce substantial subtlety.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Since $X$ is a sheafy DM stack with logarithmic structure, its functor of points on the category of logarithmic schemes is set-valued. Equivalently the diagonal morphism $(s,t) \colon R \to U \times U$ is a monomorphism. The equivalence between injectivity of relations into $U\times U$ and trivial stack structure hold for presentations of Kato--Nakayama spaces in our statement. We will use this equivalence repeatedly. 
    
    We first prove that the displayed map in (1) is injective. Suppose for contradiction that there exist two points $r_1,r_2\in |\operatorname{KN}(R)|$ which are sent to the same point $p$ of $|\operatorname{KN}(U)|\times |\operatorname{KN}(U)|$. The image of $\tau(p)\in U\times U$ in the underlying Deligne--Mumford stack $\underline{X}$ of $X$ is a closed point $q$. The gerbe structure of $\underline{X}$ at $q$ is a finite group $G_q$. According to paragraph 1 we will reach a contradiction if we show that $G_q$ acts freely on points of the Kato--Nakayama space lying over $q$.

    Since the functor of points of $X$ on the category of logarithmic schemes is setoid valued, the group $G_q$ acts freely upon standard logarithmic points lying over $q$. Note that $G_q$ acts on the pullback of $M_X$ to the closed subscheme $q$. The monoid of global sections splits $$\varphi \colon M_{q}\xrightarrow{\cong} \overline{M}_q\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times$$ because $q$ is a $\mathbb{C}$ (which is algebraically closed) valued point, and thus admits a global chart. The splitting is not canonical. Given a choice of splitting and $h\in M_q$, we write $|h|$ for the modulus of the image of $h$ under projection in $\mathbb{C}^\times$. Choosing $f\in G_q$, we will say the splitting $\varphi$ is $f$-modulus split if $|f(h)| = |h|$ for all $h$ in $M_q$. Note that in any case $f$ necessarily fixes $\mathbb{C}^\times$ because it comes from a $\mathbb{C}$ morphism of schemes. 

We claim that, after fixing a choice of $f$, it is possible to choose a splitting with respect to which $M_q$ is $f$-modulus split. Indeed, since $f$ is an automorphism and thus acts as an automorphism of $\overline{M}_q\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times/\mathbb{C}^\times$, the image of any ray in $\overline{M}_q\oplus \{1\}$ is an element of the form $(\rho,\gamma)\in \overline{M}_q\oplus\mathbb{C}^\times $ where $\rho$ is a ray. Pick an ordering on the rays $\{\rho_1,...,\rho_k\}$ of $\overline{M}_q\oplus \{1\}$ such that, up to adding an element of $\mathbb{C}^\times$, we find $f(\rho_j)$ in the set $\{\rho_1,...,\rho_{j+1}\}$. This ensures (and can be achieved by ensuring) that either $f(\rho_j,1) =(\rho_{j+1},\gamma_{j+1})$ for some $\gamma_{j+1}$ in $\mathbb{C}^\times$, or $f(\rho_j)$ is (up to the $\mathbb{C}^\times$ factor) already in the set $\{\rho_1,...,\rho_{j}\}$. We further assume that $|f(\rho_s)|=1$ for $s< r$ for some integer $r> 0$. We will inductively extend this situation to replace $r$ by $r+1$. 
    
                                                                                                                                                                                                                               
To establish the inductive step and ensure $|f(\rho_r)|=1$ we consider cases. 

    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item If under our current splitting $f(\rho_r) = (v,\gamma)$ where $v\in \overline{M}_q$ lies in the $\mathbb{Q}$-span of $\rho_1,...,\rho_{r}$, then since also $f$ permutes rays we know that $v=\rho_j$ for some $j\leq r$. Because $G_q$ is a finite group there exists a minimal integer $k$ such that $$f^k(\rho_r) = f^{k-1}(\rho_j)+\gamma= \rho_r+ \alpha$$ for some $\alpha$ in $\mathbb{C}^\times$. By the choice of ray ordering we fixed, we know that $j\leq r$. By the inductive hypothesis we have $|f^{k-1}(\rho_j)|=1$ and so $|\alpha| = |f(\rho_r)| = |\gamma|$. Since $f$ has finite order, there is some integer $w$ such that $f^{kw} = \operatorname{id}$ and so $|f^{kw}(\rho_r)| = |\rho_r| = 1$. It follows that $|\alpha|^w=1$, but $\mathbb{R}_{> 0}$ is torsion-free and so $|\alpha|=|\gamma| = 1$.\footnote{This argument does not show that we can achieve a splitting such that the argument of $f(\rho_j)=1$. This is because the multiplicative group of $\mathbb{C}$ has torsion.}
\item The only other case is that $v$ does not lie in the $\mathbb{Q}$-span of $\rho_1,...,\rho_r$. In this case we are free to alter the splitting through the automorphism characterised by sending $\rho_j\in \overline{M}_q\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times $ to $\rho_j$, unless $\rho_j=v$ where we send $v \mapsto v/\gamma$.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             
    \end{enumerate}
    
    The existence of distinct $r_1,r_2$ (fixed for contradiction in second paragraph of this proof) is equivalent to the existence of a morphism $k\colon M_q\rightarrow S^1$ extending the argument function on $\mathbb{C}^\times$, and an element $f$ of $G_q$ which fixes $k$ under precomposition. We will use these data to construct a standard log point valued point of $X$ which is invariant under $f$, thus reaching a contradiction.
    
    Choose an $f$-modulus splitting $M_q\cong \overline{M}_q\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times$ and label rays $\rho_1,...\rho_k$ of $\overline{M}_q\oplus \{1\}$. Consider a morphism $$M_q\cong \overline{M}_q\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times \rightarrow \mathbb{N}\oplus \mathbb{C}^\times$$
$$\left(\sum_i a_i \rho_i,\lambda\right) \mapsto \left(\sum_i a_i,|\lambda|k\left(\left(\sum_i a_i\rho_i,\lambda \right)\right)\right)$$
    This map is invariant under $f$ because $f$ induces a bijection from the set of rays to the set of rays, and thus the map to $\mathbb{N}$ is $f$ invariant; the argument part of the map to $\mathbb{C}^\times$ is $f$ invariant by hypothesis; the modulus part is invariant because we chose an $f$-modulus split splitting.
    We have thus specified a standard log point valued point of $X$ which is fixed by $f$. Contradiction. The displayed map in (1) is injective.

    The displayed map in (1) is proper because $|X|$ is separated. Any universally closed injection into a Hausdorff topological space is an immersion, so our map is an immersion. 
    
    We will show that the map $q\colon |\operatorname{KN}(U)|\rightarrow |\operatorname{KN}(U)|/|\operatorname{KN}(R)|$ is a local homeomorphism. The idea is to find for each point $p$ in $\operatorname{KN}(U)$ an open set $W$ containing $p$ which is mapped homeomorphically to its image - i.e. no two points distinct points in $W$ have a relation between them. Indeed, first note that the image $e$ of $U$ in $R$ is open because $U\rightarrow X$ is unramified \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02GE}{02GE}]{stacks}. Moreover, since $\operatorname{KN}(R)$ embeds in $\operatorname{KN}(U)\times \operatorname{KN}(U)$ it has the subspace topology and so there exists an open subset $T$ of $\operatorname{KN}(U)\times \operatorname{KN}(U)$ whose intersect with $\operatorname{KN}(R)$ is $e$. We can choose $W$ to be an open of $|\operatorname{KN}(U)|$ such that $W\times W$ is a subset of $T$. We claim that the restriction of $q$ to $W$ is a homeomorphism. Injectivity is immediate because we just arranged that any relation with both ends in $W$ is the identity. The map is continuous by definition of the quotient topology on $|\operatorname{KN}(U)|/|\operatorname{KN}(R)|$. 
    It remains to check that $q$ is an open map, but for $V\subset |\operatorname{KN}(U)|$ open $q^{-1}(q(V)) = t(s^{-1}(V))$, and $t$ is open because it comes from a strict \'etale map.
    
    For claim (2), it suffices to show that replacing a presentation by a refinement induces a Morita equivalent groupoid presentation, since any two presentations admit a common refinement. Concretely, let $U' \rightarrow U$ be a refined cover, and write
$$
R = U\times_X U,
\qquad
R' = U'\times_X U'.
$$
This induces a morphism of groupoid presentations
$$
\begin{tikzcd}
R' \arrow[r] \arrow[d,shift left=.5ex] \arrow[d,shift right=.5ex] & R \arrow[d,shift left=.5ex] \arrow[d,shift right=.5ex] \\
U' \arrow[r] & U.
\end{tikzcd}
$$

To check that the induced morphism
$$\left(
|\operatorname{KN}(R')| \rightrightarrows |\operatorname{KN}(U')|\right)
\longrightarrow\left(
|\operatorname{KN}(R)| \rightrightarrows |\operatorname{KN}(U)|\right)
$$
is a Morita equivalence we first verify full faithfulness: we have
$
R'
\cong
U'\times_U R\times_U U',
$
so preservation of fibre products by the Kato--Nakayama functor over strict morphisms \cite[Proposition~3.1]{cailotto2004katonakayama} gives
$$
|\operatorname{KN}(R')|
\cong
|\operatorname{KN}(U')|
\times_{|\operatorname{KN}(U)|}
|\operatorname{KN}(R)|
\times_{|\operatorname{KN}(U)|}
|\operatorname{KN}(U')|,
$$
but this is what it means to be fully faithful.

We now argue that the induced morphism is essentially surjective. Indeed the map
$
|\operatorname{KN}(U')|\to |\operatorname{KN}(U)|
$
is surjective and open because $U'\to U$ is surjective and strict étale. 
                                                                                                                                                                                                              
Surjectivity ensures that every point $u\in |\operatorname{KN}(U)|$ lifts to $u'\in |\operatorname{KN}(U')|$ and then $(u',\mathrm{id}_u)$ is a point of
$
|\operatorname{KN}(U')|
\times_{|\operatorname{KN}(U)|}
|\operatorname{KN}(R)|
$
with image $u$.
Claim (3) is descent of sheaves and morphisms along a strict \'etale open cover.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
\label{defn:logFG}
 Let $X$ be a separated complex logarithmic space which admits a choice $q\colon X'\rightarrow X$ of logarithmic alteration by a sheafy DM stack with locally free logarithmic structure which is of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. The $k^\mathsf{th}$ homotopy group of $X$ is the $k^{\mathsf{th}}$ homotopy group of the Kato--Nakayama space $\mathsf{KN}(X')$.
Let $S$ be the standard logarithmic point.
The relative homotopy groups of a morphism of logarithmic spaces $X\rightarrow S$ are defined as the kernel $$\pi_k(\mathsf{KN}_0(X)) := \mathsf{Ker}(\pi_k(\mathsf{KN}(X))\rightarrow \pi_k(\mathsf{KN}(S))).$$
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:HomotopyGroups}
    The logarithmic homotopy groups in Definition~\ref{defn:logFG} of a logarithmic space $X$ of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ are well defined independent of the choice of logarithmic alteration $X'\rightarrow X$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:NerveStuff}
    Applying the Kato--Nakayama functor to the nerve of a sheafy DM stack with locally free logarithmic structure $Y$ satisfying the hypotheses above yields our simplicial space with the following properties.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item The natural map between the two topological realisations of a simplicial space described in \cite[Appendix A]{SEGAL1974293} is a homotopy equivalence.
        \item This common homotopy type of (1) coincides with the homotopy type of $\operatorname{KN}(Y)$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By \cite[Proposition A.1(iv)]{SEGAL1974293}, (1) will follow once we show that our nerve is good in the sense of \cite[Definition A.4]{SEGAL1974293}. To show that a simplicial space is good we check that for each $s$ the inclusion of the image of $\operatorname{KN}(R_{s-1})$ in $\operatorname{KN}(R_{s})$ under each degeneracy map is a closed cofibration. We will show more: this inclusion is both closed and open, thus is the inclusion of a union of connected components.
    
    Since the map $\tau\colon \operatorname{KN}(R_{s})\rightarrow R_s^{an}$ is continuous, it will suffice to check that the image of $R_{s-1}^{an}$ in $R_{s}^{an}$ is both closed and open. Moreover, it suffices to check that the image of $R_{s-1}$ in $R_{s}$ is closed and open because the Zariski topology has fewer open sets than the analytic topology.

    Openness follows by \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02GE}{02GE}]{stacks} because the map $U\rightarrow Y$ is (strict) \'etale and thus unramified. The image is closed because $U\rightarrow Y$ is separated which is by definition the same as the map $U\rightarrow U\times_YU$ being a closed immersion, see \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03HL}{03HL}]{stacks} and \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04XB}{04XB}]{stacks}.

    It remains to prove (2). Indeed the map $U\rightarrow Y$ is strict and so the fibre products in the definitions of $R_i$ commute with the Kato--Nakayama functor by \cite[Proposition~3.1]{cailotto2004katonakayama}. Thus the nerve of $R_1\rightarrow R_2$ is sent to the nerve of $\operatorname{KN}(R_1)\rightarrow \operatorname{KN}(R_2)$. Claim (2) follows because the Cech nerve of a local homeomorphism realises the homotopy type of a space by \cite[Corollary 1.5]{MR2045835}
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Any two logarithmic alterations $X',X''\rightarrow X$ admit a common refinement $X'\times_XX''$. Subdividing further we may assume this logarithmic alteration has locally free logarithmic structure. In the rest of this proof all logarithmic schemes are assumed to have locally free logarithmic structure. It will suffice to verify that for any sheafy DM stack with logarithmic structure $Y$, the isomorphism classes of the logarithmic homotopy groups are invariant under logarithmic alteration $Y'\rightarrow Y$. 
    
    Note that any logarithmic alteration $Y'\rightarrow Y$ can be factored $$Y'\rightarrow \overline{Y}\rightarrow Y$$ where the first map is a change of lattice and the second is a (possibly not projective) logarithmic modification. We now argue that it will suffice to handle the case that this second logarithmic modification is projective. Indeed after replacing $\overline{Y}$ by a log modification $\overline{Y}'$ which is projective over $Y$, and $Y'$ by $\widetilde{Y} = \overline{Y}'\times_{\overline{Y}}Y'$, both of the maps $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y$ and $\widetilde{Y}\rightarrow Y'$ have this projectivity property.\footnote{See for example \cite[Prop 5.5.5 (v)]{EGA2}.} We can thus deduce the general case after we establish both the case that $Y'\rightarrow Y$ is a log blowup, and the case that $Y'\rightarrow Y$ is a Kummer root stack.
    
    We first handle the case that $Y$ is a scheme with logarithmic structure.
    Following the previous paragraph, we may assume that $Y'\rightarrow Y$ is either a log blowup or a root stack. The isomorphism class of the logarithmic homotopy groups to a fine and saturated logarithmic scheme $
    Y$ is invariant under logarithmic blowups 
    \cite[Proposition 9.3.5]{binda2025logarithmicmotivichomotopytheory}. 
    It is immediate from the definition of root stack presented in \cite[Definition~2.2.6.2]{MolchoWise} that passing to the root stack does not change the isomorphism type of the topological Kato--Nakayama space (because the group $S^1$ is divisible).

    In the case that $Y$ is a DM stack with logarithmic structure which is not a scheme with logarithmic structure, choose a strict \'etale groupoid presentation $s,t\colon R_2 = U\times_{Y} U \rightrightarrows R_1 = U$ of $Y$ where $U$ and $R_2$ are schemes as in the paragraph preceding Lemma \ref{lem:NerveStuff}. Base changing this presentation along the map $Y'\rightarrow Y$ yields a strict \'etale groupoid presentation of $Y'$, say $R_2'=U'\times_{Y'} U' \rightrightarrows U'$ where $R_1'=U'$ and $R_s'$ are DM stacks with logarithmic structure. The morphisms $R_i'\rightarrow R_i$ are the base change of a logarithmic alteration, and since for all $i$ we know that $R_i$ is a scheme with logarithmic structure it follows from the previous paragraph that these maps induce a logarithmic homotopy equivalence i.e. a homotopy equivalence on the level of Kato--Nakayama spaces. By Lemma \ref{lem:NerveStuff}(2) we have a homotopy equivalence at every level of the nerve of the Kato--Nakayama spaces of $Y$ and $Y'$, and the claim follows from \cite[Proposition A.1(ii)]{SEGAL1974293} together with Lemma \ref{lem:NerveStuff}(2).
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:Serre Fibration}
    Let $X\rightarrow Y$ be a saturated, proper,\footnote{We follow the algebro--geometric convention that any proper map is separated. Separatedness is stated as a separate condition in \cite[Theorem~5.1]{NakayamaOgus2010RelativeRounding} where the authors often appeal to results in the topological category where conventions differ.} and logarithmically smooth morphism of sheafy DM stacks with locally free logarithmic structure. Assume that $Y$ is separated and of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. Then the map $$|\mathsf{KN}(X)|\rightarrow |\mathsf{KN}(Y)|$$ is a Serre fibration.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
If $X$ and $Y$ were schemes with logarithmic structure we could deduce from \cite[Theorem~5.1]{NakayamaOgus2010RelativeRounding} that the morphism $\mathsf{KN}(X)\rightarrow \mathsf{KN}(Y)$ is a fibre bundle. To extend this claim to the situation that $X,Y$ are sheafy DM stacks with logarithmic structure recall that the proof of \textit{loc. cit.} proceeds by checking that the morphism of Kato--Nakayama spaces is a proper (separated) topological submersion. Being a topological submersion can be checked locally, and the local situation is unchanged when studying the Kato--Nakayama space of a sheafy DM stack with logarithmic structure because we  saw in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemdefn:KNSpace} that the map $|\operatorname{KN}(U)|\rightarrow |\operatorname{KN}(U)|/|\operatorname{KN}(R)|$ is a local homeomorphism of topological spaces. Properness descends along finite proper maps by the argument of \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03GN}{03GN}]{stacks}.
    It remains to note that the target is paracompact and Hausdorff (follows directly from construction of \cite[Section~1]{KatoNakayama1999}) and so the result follows by \cite[Theorem, Section~7.4]{May1999Concise}.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:NeedRelative}
    The topological Kato--Nakayama space of a standard logarithmic point is $ S^1$, and in particular has non-trivial fundamental group. It thus follows from Lemma \ref{lem:Serre Fibration} that any scheme which is exact, proper, and logarithmically smooth over a standard logarithmic point has non-trivial logarithmic fundamental group.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
Let $X\rightarrow S$ be a morphism of Deligne--Mumford stacks with logarithmic structure of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$. 
We denote the sheaf of kummer \'etale logarithmic differential 1-forms of \cite[3.8]{IllusieKatoNakayama2005} by $\omega_{X/S}^1$ and the associated logarithmic de Rham complex by $\omega_{X/S}^\bullet$ (also defined in \cite[3.8]{IllusieKatoNakayama2005}).
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{defn:cotangent}
    Let $X\rightarrow S$ be a logarithmically smooth morphism of Noetherian Deligne--Mumford stacks with logarithmic structure. The \textit{relative logarithmic tangent bundle} $T_{X/S}^{\operatorname{log}}$ is the vector bundle dual to $\omega^1_{X/S}$.
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{defn:Perfectpair}
    Let $X/\Delta_0$ be a smooth morphism of Noetherian DM stacks with logarithmic structure. An element $\eta$ of $H^0(X,\omega_{X/\Delta_0}^2)$ is nowhere degenerate if it induces an isomorphism from the logarithmic tangent bundle to the logarithmic cotangent bundle $$T_{X/\Delta_0}^{\operatorname{log}}\rightarrow \omega_{X/\Delta_0}^1.$$
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
\label{defn:PerfectPair}
    Let $\Delta_0$ be the standard logarithmic point.\footnote{It suffices that $\Delta_0$ is static in the sense of \cite[Section 2]{logcoh}.} Let $X\rightarrow \Delta_0$ be a morphism of logarithmic spaces which is locally logarithmically smooth, and assume that $X$ admits a logarithmic alteration which is a Noetherian DM stack with logarithmic structure. We define a \textit{logarithmic k form}, or equivalently a \textit{global section of $\omega_{X'/\Delta_0}^k$}, to be an equivalence class of pairs $(q\colon X'\rightarrow X, \eta')$ where $X'\rightarrow X$ is any logarithmic alteration with domain a Noetherian DM stack with a logarithmically smooth logarithmic structure, and $\eta' \in H^0(X',\omega^k_{X/\Delta_0})$. The equivalence relation is pullback along refinements of logarithmic alterations. We say that a logarithmic 2-form $[(q\colon X'\rightarrow X, \eta')]$ is \textit{nowhere degenerate} if for some choice of $q$ the form $\eta'$ is nowhere degenerate in the sense of Definition \ref{defn:Perfectpair}.
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- remark-11: body_md -->
The logarithmic cotangent bundle is same data as a locally free coherent sheaf in the logarithmic \'etale topology. A logarithmic two form is a global section of this sheaf, and nowhere degenerate means that the induced morphism from the logarithmic tangent bundle to the logarithmic cotangent bundle is an isomorphism of logarithmic coherent sheaves. More precisely, one defines the logarithmic cotangent bundle by applying the up functor of \cite[Section 1]{logcoh} to $\omega^2_{X'}$ for any choice of $X'$.
<!-- end remark-11 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
Definition \ref{defn:PerfectPair} is well defined independent of the logarithmic alteration ${X}\rightarrow X$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
Since each element in the equivalence class $X'\rightarrow S$ is logarithmically smooth, we know each possible representative of $\omega_{X/S}$ is locally free. Moreover, $S$ is static and thus for every representative $X'\rightarrow S$ which is logarithmically smooth, we know that $X'$ is static. Locally free sheaves on static logarithmic schemes satisfy descent in the full logarithmic \'etale topology by \cite[Section 2]{logcoh} and the result is proved.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
\label{defn:LogIHS}
    We say that a proper and locally logarithmically smooth morphism  $X\rightarrow S$ of logarithmic spaces is a family of logarithmic IHS varieties if the following hypotheses are satisfied whenever $\mathcal{X}_p$ is the base change of $X\rightarrow S$ along any standard logarithmic point $p$ of $S$.
     \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
         \item \textbf{Logarithmic simply connected.} The morphism of logarithmic fundamental groups $$\pi_1^{\operatorname{log}}(\mathcal{X}_p)\rightarrow \pi_1^{\operatorname{log}}(\Delta_0)$$ has trivial kernel and the morphism $X\rightarrow S$ has geometrically connected fibres.
         \item \textbf{Logarithmic symplectic structure.} The cohomology of the space $\mathcal{X}_p$ has the property $$H^{2,0}_{\log}(\mathcal X_p,\mathbb{C}) := H^0(\mathcal X_p,\omega_{\mathcal X_p/p}^2) = \mathbb{C}\eta$$ where $\eta$ is nowhere degenerate.
         \item \textbf{Projective up to logarithmic alteration.} There exists a logarithmic alteration of $\mathcal{X}_p$ which admits an ample polarisation (and is thus a DM stack with projective coarse moduli space).
     \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
An integral affine manifold $B$ of dimension $m$ is an $m$-dimensional topological manifold $\underline{B}$ together with an equivalence class of atlases $$U_i\rightarrow \underline{B} \text{ and charts } \psi_i\colon U_i \xrightarrow{\cong} V_i$$
    where $U_i\rightarrow \underline{B}$ forms an open cover, each $V_i\subset M_m\otimes \mathbb{R}$ is a connected open subset, $\psi_i$ is a homeomorphism, and $$\psi_j \circ \psi_i^{-1}\colon \psi_i(U_i \cap U_j) \rightarrow V_j \text{ is the restriction of some } h \in \operatorname{Aff}(M_m).$$ The equivalence relation identifies atlases whose union is also an atlas. A morphism of integral affine manifolds $B\rightarrow B'$ is a morphism of topological manifolds $\underline{f}\colon \underline{B}\rightarrow \underline{B}'$ such that the induced map $$\psi_i'\circ \underline{f} \circ\psi_j^{-1}\colon V_i\rightarrow V_j'$$ is locally the restriction of an element in $M_{\operatorname{dim}(B')} \rtimes \operatorname{Hom}(M_{\operatorname{dim}(B)},M_{\operatorname{dim}(B')})$.
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
\label{defn:IASsing}
    An \textit{integral affine manifold with singularities (IAMS) of dimension $m$} $(B,D)$ is an $m$-dimensional topological manifold $B$, a closed subset $D\subset B$ called the \textit{singular locus} which locally can be written as a finite union of manifolds of codimension at least two, and an integral affine manifold $B_0$ with underlying topological manifold $\underline{B}_0 = B\backslash D.$ An isomorphism of IAMS is an isomorphism of topological manifolds $B\rightarrow B'$ which identifies singular loci, and which induces an isomorphism of integral affine manifolds $B_0\rightarrow B_0'$.
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
\label{defn:IAMWithSing}
    The phrase \textit{a family of integral affine manifolds with singularities over the rational polyhedral cone $\sigma$} refers to any of the following constructions, which we introduce in the following sections: 
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item Families of tropical abelian varieties over $\sigma$ (Definition~\ref{defn:TropicalAV}).
        \item The (relative) tropical Hilbert scheme of points on a tropical abelian variety over $\sigma$ (Definition~\ref{defn:TropHilb}).
        \item Families of tropical generalised Kummer varieties over $\sigma$ (Definition~\ref{defn:TropGenKummer}).
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- remark-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:IAMSB}
    With two exceptions, we will explain how points in the base of a family of integral affine manifolds with singularities specify an IAMS in the sense of Definition \ref{defn:IASsing}. The exceptions are the structures which type II degenerations of Hilbert schemes of points and generalised Kummer varieties give rise to. This structure is not an integral affine manifold with singularities - in the generalised Kummer case it is homeomorphic to a simplex, and satisfies the obvious definition of an \textit{integral affine manifold with boundary}. We do not suggest such a definition because it is not required to prove any of our theorems.
<!-- end remark-12 -->
<!-- remark-13: body_md -->
We do not attempt to formulate general axioms for our perspective on families of integral affine manifolds. Although we anticipate such language will eventually become desirable, it is not required for the arguments of this paper. We note that this speculative definition would generalise the category of piecewise linear spaces introduced in \cite[Section 1]{LogQuot}: subdivisions of a cone complex with domain a piecewise linear space biject with those monomorphisms with codomain a cone complex which induce a bijection on points.
<!-- end remark-13 -->
<!-- remark-14: body_md -->
Whilst moduli of tropical abelian varieties have been extensively studied, a significant section of the moduli of tropical abelian variety literature does not characterise a family of tropical abelian varieties as a family of integral affine manifolds. Exceptions include an implicit definition in the work of Kajiwara, Kato, and Nakayama \cite{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008}, which is made explicit in recent work, see \cite[Definition~3.4]{botero2026pureextensionthetadivisor}, \cite{FeusiLopezTropAV}, and \cite[Definition~3.5]{FeusiMolchoOrbifoldCompactifiedJacobians}.
<!-- end remark-14 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
In this paper we are led to study families of integral affine manifolds with singularities because, in constructing $\mathcal{K}_{2n}$ and its universal family, we consider generalised Kummer varieties over a base fine and saturated logarithmic scheme $S$ of any dimension, and with logarithmic structure of any rank. In the case that $S=\Delta$, and thus the Artin fan of $S$ is $a^\ast \sigma = a^\ast \mathbb{N}$, it is not necessary to work with families of integral affine manifolds.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:DataIAMS}
    An IAMS $(B,D)$ of dimension $n$ is determined by its underlying topological manifold $B$, the singular locus $D\subset B$, and the sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{B_0}\subset C^0(\underline{B}_0)$ of integral affine functions on $\underline{B}_0 = B \backslash D$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Choose an open cover of $\underline{B}_0$ by simply connected sets $U_i\rightarrow \underline{B}_0$. Refining the cover if necessary, we may further assume that sections of the quotient sheaf $\mathcal{O}_{B_0}/C$ on each $U_i$ are isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}^{n}$. 
    Since each $U_i$ is simply connected $H^1(U_i,\mathbb{Z})=0$, and thus any basis of $\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal{O}_{B_0}/C)$ admits a lift to a tuple of sections of $\mathcal{O}_{B_0}(U_i)$. This lift determines a map from $U_i$ to $\mathbb{R}^n$, and we choose an identification $\mathbb{R}^n \cong M_n\otimes \mathbb{R}$. Working chart locally on $U_i$ (with charts on our favourite atlas) we can apply the inverse function theorem to deduce that this map is a local homeomorphism. After replacing $U_i$ with a smaller open subset we have defined an immersion of integral affine manifolds $\psi_i\colon U_i\rightarrow M_n\otimes \mathbb{R}$. In particular, we have constructed an atlas, and thus the IAM structure on $B_0$ is determined.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-25: body_md -->
An element $\phi$ of $\mathsf{Hom}(\textbf{X},\mathsf{Hom}(\sigma,\mathbb{Z}))$ is said to have \textit{bounded monodromy} (with respect to $\varphi$) if for each $x$ in $\textbf{X}$ there exist $y,y'$ in $\textbf{Y}$ such that, $$Q_{\varphi}(x,y) \leq \phi(x) \leq Q_{\varphi}(x,y').$$ We write $\mathsf{Hom}(\textbf{X},\mathsf{Hom}(\sigma,\mathbb{Z}))^{(\textbf{Y})}$ for the subgroup of bounded monodromy elements.
<!-- end definition-25 -->
<!-- definition-26: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropicalAV}
    Let $\mathpzc{A}(\varphi)$ be the group sheaf on $\textbf{RPC}_\sigma$ whose $\kappa/\sigma$ valued points are elements of $$\mathsf{Hom}(\textbf{X},\mathsf{Hom}(\kappa,\mathbb{Z}))^{(\textbf{Y})}/\textbf{Y},$$ and where pullback along $\kappa\rightarrow \kappa'$ is induced in the obvious way. A \textit{tropical abelian variety over} $\sigma$ is any sheaf on $\textbf{RPC}_\sigma$ isomorphic to $\mathpzc{A}(\varphi)/\sigma$ where $\varphi$ satisfies the following \textit{polarisability hypothesis}: There exists a morphism $\Phi\colon \textbf{Y} \rightarrow \textbf{X}$ with finite cokernel such that the induced bilinear form $Q_{\varphi}(\Phi(-),-)$ is symmetric and positive semi-definite (i.e. the image function is non-negative on $\sigma$).
<!-- end definition-26 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:FunctorPointsTropAV}

There exists a tropical model $$j\colon \Lambda \rightarrow \mathpzc{A}(\varphi).$$
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
This is \cite[Theorem~5.2.1]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- definition-27: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropAVPolarised}
    Let $\sigma$ be a rational polyhedral cone. A principally polarised tropical abelian variety over $\sigma$ is the data of a tropical abelian variety equipped with an isomorphism $\lambda\colon \mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^\vee$ which is symmetric (i.e. equal to its dual under the identification $(\mathpzc{A}^\vee)^\vee \cong \mathpzc{A}$) and satisfies a positivity condition (see \cite[Definition 4.3]{FeusiLopezTropAV} for details).
<!-- end definition-27 -->
<!-- definition-28: body_md -->
\label{defn:ModuliIAMAbVar}
    Let $$\varphi \colon \textbf{Y}\rightarrow \mathsf{Hom}(\textbf{X},\mathsf{Hom}(\rho,\mathbb{Z}))$$ be a group homomorphism such that there is an isomorphism of group sheaves over $\rho$ $\mathpzc{A}(\varphi) \cong \mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho$. The \textit{integral affine manifold $B(\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho/\rho)$ associated to the pair} $(\rho\rightarrow \sigma, \mathpzc{A}/\sigma)$ is defined to be $\mathsf{Hom}(\textbf{X},\mathsf{Hom}(\rho,\mathbb{Z}))^{(\textbf{Y})}\otimes \mathbb{R}/\varphi(\textbf{Y})$. Whenever we have fixed a presentation $\mathpzc{A}(\varphi) = \mathpzc{A}$, we can abbreviate $B(\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho) = B(\varphi)$.
<!-- end definition-28 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
The integral affine manifold $B(\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho/\rho)$ is independent of the choice of $\varphi$.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The underlying topological space of $B(\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho/\rho)$ is the link to the morphism $\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma\rho \rightarrow \rho$. By Lemma \ref{lem:DataIAMS} it remains to identify its sheaf of integral affine functions. A base $\{\iota\colon U_\iota\hookrightarrow B(\varphi)\}$ for the topology of the link is indexed by injective kummer-free maps over $\rho$, $$\iota \colon \tau \hookrightarrow \mathpzc{A}(\varphi)$$ from cones $\tau/\rho$ of dimension $\mathsf{dim}(|\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \rho|)\leq g+1$.
    The open set $U_\iota$ is the intersection of the preimage of $1\in \rho$ with the image of the interior of $|\tau \otimes \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}|$ under $|\iota\otimes \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}|$.
    The sheaf of integral affine functions is defined by declaring its sections on the open set $U_\iota$ to be $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau,\mathbb{Z})$. There is a natural inclusion of $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau,\mathbb{Z})$ into the set of continuous functions on $U_\iota$: indeed $U_\iota$ is a subset of the preimage of $1\in \rho$ and thus pulls back to a subset of $\tau$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- example-4: body_md -->
Suppose $\textbf{X},\textbf{Y} \cong \mathbb{Z}$ have rank $1$ and $\sigma=\mathbb{N}^2$. We specify a family of tropical abelian varieties through the map $$\begin{aligned}
\varphi\colon \textbf{Y} = \mathbb{Z} 
&\longrightarrow \mathbb{Z}^2 
  = \mathsf{Hom}\bigl(\mathbb{Z}, \mathsf{Hom}(\mathbb{N}^2,\mathbb{Z})\bigr) \\
u 
&\longmapsto (3u, 0).
\end{aligned}$$ 
Given a ray $\rho = (\alpha, \beta)$ in $\sigma$ write $\varphi_\rho$ for the base changed tropical abelian variety. Then for $\alpha \ne 0$, $B(\varphi_\rho)$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{R}$ by $3 \alpha\mathbb{Z}$, but $B(\varphi_\rho)$ is zero in the special case that $\alpha=0$.
<!-- end example-4 -->
<!-- definition-29: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropAVLevel}(Feusi--L\'opez \cite{FeusiLopezTropAV})
    A level $m$ structure on a tropical abelian variety $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \sigma$ is a surjection of group objects on $\textbf{RPC}_\sigma$ $$\pi_m\colon  [m]^\ast \textbf{V}\twoheadrightarrow [m]^\ast \mathpzc{A}[m].$$ For every test object $\tau/\sigma \in \textbf{RPC}_\sigma$ we require that $\ker(\pi_m)(\tau) \subseteq V$ is a coisotropic subgroup isomorphic as an abstract group to $(\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^{r_\tau}$ for some $g \leq r_\tau \leq 2g$.
<!-- end definition-29 -->
<!-- definition-30: body_md -->
The moduli space of principally polarised tropical abelian varieties with level $m$ structure $\mathfrak{A}_g(m)$ is the stack on \textbf{RPC} whose $\sigma$ valued points are principally polarised tropical abelian varieties over $\sigma$ with level $m$ structure. We write $\mathpzc{Y}(m)\rightarrow \mathfrak{A}_g(m)$ for its universal tropical abelian variety.
<!-- end definition-30 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:TropAVModel}
    For each integer $m\geq 3$ there are (infinitely many) choices of diagram with horizontal arrows tropical models 
    $$ 
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathpzc{Y}_{\Lambda}(m) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
  & \mathpzc{Y}(m) \arrow[d] \\
\mathfrak{A}_{g,\Lambda}(m) \arrow[r] 
  & \mathfrak{A}_g(m),
\end{tikzcd}
    $$
    and the left hand vertical map is an integral morphism of cone complexes.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
See \cite{FeusiLopezTropAV}.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- definition-31: body_md -->
Let $\mathpzc{T}$ be a sheaf on \textbf{RPC} which admits a tropical model. A locally closed stratification $\mathcal{P}$ of $|\mathscr{T}|$ is \textit{conical} if $\mathscr{T}$ admits a tropical model such that each stratum of $\mathcal{P}$ is a union of interiors of cones.
<!-- end definition-31 -->
<!-- definition-32: body_md -->
\label{defn:weightedPLSUBDiv}
An $m$-\textit{weighted zero-dimensional piecewise linear subdivision} of a family $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \sigma$ of tropical abelian varieties (resp. of the projection $\mathbb{R}^k\times \sigma\rightarrow \sigma$) is a pair $$(\mathcal{P},w\colon \mathcal{P}\rightarrow \mathbb{N})$$ where,
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
    \item The first element of our tuple $\mathcal{P}$ is a conical stratification of $|\mathpzc{A}|$ (resp of $|\mathbb{R}^k \times \sigma|$) such that the image of each stratum of $\mathcal{P}$ in $|\sigma|$ is the entire interior of a face.
    \item There exist $m$ sections $(s_1,..,s_m)$ of $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \sigma$ (resp. $\mathbb{R}^k\times \sigma \rightarrow \sigma$) such that:
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
      \item The stratification $\mathcal{P}$ is the common refinement of the stratification pulled back from $\sigma$, and the stratification defined by the image of the $s_i$.
      \item The function $w$ is defined by $$w(\alpha)=\operatorname{card}\left(\{i:\alpha\subseteq |s_i(\sigma)|\}\right).$$ 
    \end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-32 -->
<!-- definition-33: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropHilb}
    Let $\mathpzc{A}/\sigma$ be a tropical abelian variety. The \textit{tropical Hilbert scheme} $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}/\sigma$ of $\mathpzc{A}/\sigma$ is the sheaf on \textbf{RPC}$/\sigma$ whose $\kappa\rightarrow \sigma$ valued points are families of $(n+1)$-weighted zero-dimensional piecewise linear subdivisions of $\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \kappa$ over $\kappa$. The \textit{universal tropical subscheme} $\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}(\mathpzc{A})$ is defined through its functor of points, whose value on a test object $\tau$ is the subset of $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau,\mathpzc{A}\times_\sigma \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]})$ with the following property. First note that a map to $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$ definitionally determines a conical locally closed stratification of $\tau\times_\sigma \mathpzc{A}$. Our condition is that the image of $\tau$ in $\tau\times_\sigma \mathpzc{A}$ is contained within the union of strata of positive weight.
<!-- end definition-33 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
One can define the stack of tropical supports of $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \sigma$ as the CFG over $\textbf{RPC}_\sigma$ whose $\tau\rightarrow \sigma$ valued points are monomorphisms in the category of sheaves on \textbf{RPC} $$\iota \colon \mathscr{T}\rightarrow \tau \times_{\sigma} \mathpzc{A}$$ satisfying:
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
        \item A flatness condition (parallel to \cite[Definition~1.3.3]{LogQuot})
        \item The morphism $\iota$ is represented in the category of piecewise linear spaces, see \cite[Section~1]{LogQuot}. 
    \end{enumerate}
    There is a canonical map from $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$ as defined here to the above stack of tropical supports. The current perspective differs in two, essentially cosmetic, ways. First, since this paper works with Hilbert schemes of points, it suffices to concern ourselves with $\mathcal{P}$ arising from a collection of sections. Second, strata track a weight $w$ which is closely related to K-tropicalisation as discussed in \cite{Quot2}.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:ModelOfAn}
    There exist (infinitely many) choices of tropical model $$\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$$ and for each such choice the fibre product $$\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}):=\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}(\mathpzc{A}) \rightarrow  \mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}(\mathpzc{A})$$ is a tropical model which is exact over $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$.
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
We will first argue that $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$ admits a tropical model. Let $\overline{\mathpzc{A}}\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}$ be a tropical model as in Lemma~\ref{lem:FunctorPointsTropAV}.
    The fibre product $\overline{\mathpzc{A}}^{n+1}$ of $n+1$ copies of $\overline{\mathpzc{A}}/\sigma$ taken over $\sigma$ remains a cone complex. The $\kappa\rightarrow \sigma$ valued points are ordered tuples of $n+1$ sections $\{(s_1,...,s_{n+1})\}$ of $\overline{\mathpzc{A}}\times_\sigma \kappa\rightarrow \kappa$. Let $\Sigma'$ be a subdivision of $\mathpzc{A}^{n+1}$ such that on the interior of each cone the set of pairs $(i,j)$ such that $s_i = s_j$ is constant - such a subdivision exists because the stratification by locus where $s_i= s_j$ is conical in the sense of \cite[Section~1.2.1]{LogQuot}. By \cite[Proposition~1.2.5, Lemma~1.5.4]{LogQuot} and \cite{MR2248429}, $\Sigma'$ admits a $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ equivariant subdivision. This subdivision descends to a subdivision $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)$ of the coarse space to the stack quotient $[\mathpzc{A}^{n+1}/\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)]$. To see that $\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$ is a cone complex note that the cone complex structure is induced by the sections used to define the locally closed stratification $\mathcal{P}^{[n+1]}$. Exactness requires showing that the image of each cone is an entire cone, but the projection of the image of a section is certainly the entire cone.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:HilbPtsOverA2}
    Let $n\geq 2$. There is a diagram with horizontal arrows tropical models 
    $$ 
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathpzc{Y}_{\Lambda}^{[n+1]}(n+1) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
  & \mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1) \arrow[d] \\
\mathfrak{A}_{g,\Lambda}(n+1) \arrow[r] 
  & \mathfrak{A}_g(n+1).
\end{tikzcd}
    $$
    and the left hand vertical map is an integral morphism of cone complexes.
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
To begin, choose any tropical model $\Lambda \rightarrow \mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)$ which exists by Proposition~\ref{prop:TropAVModel}. For each maximal cone $\sigma$ of $\Lambda$ choose a subdivision of $\mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1)\times_{\mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)}\sigma$, which exists by Proposition~\ref{prop:ModelOfAn}. We obtain a piecewise linear space $\mathscr{T}$ subdividing $\mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1)\times_{\mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)}\Lambda$ as follows. It will suffice to specify compatible piecewise linear subdivisions of $$\mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1)\times_{\mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)}\sigma$$ induced by pullback along the map $\sigma \rightarrow \Lambda$. Such a piecewise linear subdivision is induced by a conical locally closed stratification: we take the common refinement over all choices of maximal cone $\kappa \rightarrow \Lambda$ of the locally closed stratification of $$\mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1)\times_{\mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)}\sigma\times_{\mathfrak{A}_g(n+1)} \kappa$$ induced by the choice made in the second sentence of this paragraph.

    The resulting piecewise linear space $\mathscr{T}$ admits a tropical model $\Lambda'$ by \cite[Proposition 1.2.5]{LogQuot}. We thus have a diagram with horizontal maps tropical models,$$ 
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathpzc{Y}_{\Lambda}^{[n+1]}(n+1) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
  & \mathpzc{Y}^{[n+1]}(n+1) \arrow[d] \\
\mathfrak{A}_{g,\Lambda}(n+1) \arrow[r] 
  & \mathfrak{A}_g(n+1).
\end{tikzcd}
    $$
    Applying toric semistable reduction \cite{molcho2019universal} to the morphism on the left yields the required diagram.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- definition-34: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropGenKummer} The \textit{tropical generalised Kummer variety} $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ associated to a tropical abelian variety $\mathpzc{A}$ over a cone $\sigma$ is the fibre product in the category of sheaves on $\textbf{RPC}_\sigma$,
$$\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}) \arrow[d] \arrow[r] & \sigma \arrow[d, "0", hook] \\
{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}} \arrow[r]                           & \mathpzc{A}
\end{tikzcd}.$$
<!-- end definition-34 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:KummerSubdivision}
    There are (infinitely many) choices of tropical model
    $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$$ and for each such choice the fibre product $$\mathpzc{Z}_{K}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}):=\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\times_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})}\mathpzc{Z}_{K}(\mathpzc{A}) \rightarrow  \mathpzc{Z}_{K}(\mathpzc{A})$$
    is a tropical model.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
We will show existence of such a tropical model. The second clause follows identically to the proof of Proposition~\ref{prop:ModelOfAn}. 
    
    Fix a choice of tropical model $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}$ whose existence is guaranteed by Proposition~\ref{prop:ModelOfAn}, and choose also a tropical model $\overline{\mathpzc{A}}\rightarrow\mathpzc{A}$.
    Note that the summation morphism on the sections defining $\mathcal{P}^{[n+1]}$ defines a map $\Sigma_{\operatorname{trop}}\colon \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}$.
    Let $|e|$ be the image of the identity section of $\mathpzc{A}/\sigma$ in $|\mathpzc{A}|$, and note that $\{\Sigma_{\operatorname{trop}}^{-1}(|e|), |\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}| \backslash \Sigma_{\operatorname{trop}}^{-1}(|e|)\}$ pulls back along the first projection to a conical locally closed stratification of $|\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times\mathpzc{A}|$, and thus of $|\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)\times\overline{\mathpzc{A}}|$.
    By \cite[Proposition 1.2.5]{LogQuot} such a conical locally closed subdivision of a cone complex defines a subdivision of piecewise linear spaces $\mathpzc{T}\rightarrow {\mathpzc{A}}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)\times\overline{\mathpzc{A}}$. By \cite[Lemma~1.5.4]{LogQuot} there exists a tropical model $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times\mathpzc{A}(\Lambda)\rightarrow \mathpzc{T}$. After replacing $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)$ by a subdivision, we may assume that the morphism $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times\mathpzc{A}(\Lambda) \rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)$ is integral. Indeed the new subdivision is obtained by replacing our non-integral map with its stacky toric semistable reduction \cite{molcho2019universal}. Having updated $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)$ in this way we obtain the required tropical model $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}):= \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda) \rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$$ 
    because the canonical morphism $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\hookrightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}(\Lambda)$ is the inclusion of a sub-cone complex.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
Let $n\geq 2$. There is a diagram with horizontal arrows tropical models 
    $$ 
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{Y}(n+1)) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] 
  & \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{Y}(n+1)) \arrow[d] \\
\mathfrak{A}_{g,\Lambda}(n+1) \arrow[r] 
  & \mathfrak{A}_g(n+1).
\end{tikzcd}
    $$
    and the left hand vertical map is an integral morphism of cone complexes.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Follows from Proposition~\ref{prop:KummerSubdivision} by the argument used to deduce Lemma~\ref{lem:HilbPtsOverA2} from Proposition~\ref{prop:ModelOfAn}
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:description link}
    There is a homeomorphism between the link of the map $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})\rightarrow \rho$$ and the closed subspace of $\operatorname{Sym}^{n+1}(B(\mathpzc{A}/\rho))$ specifying unordered tuples of $n+1$ points which sum to zero in the group law of $B(\mathpzc{A}/\rho)$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Apply the topological realisation functor to the square of Definition~\ref{defn:TropGenKummer} (setting $\sigma =\rho$), and note it remains cartesian as a diagram in the category of topological spaces.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- definition-35: body_md -->
\label{defn:IAMSGenKum}
    Let $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \rho$ be a tropical abelian variety of relative dimension two over a ray. There is an IAMS (possibly with boundary), denoted $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$, associated to $$\pi \colon  \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})\rightarrow \rho$$ which is defined as follows.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
    \item The underlying topological space is the link of $\pi$.

    \item The codimension two singular locus $D\subset B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ consists of points where at least two of $(s_1,...,s_{n+1})$ coincide. 

    \item The integral affine structure on $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})\backslash D$ is specified by the affine functions on a base for the topology. A base is indexed by kummer-free injective maps with domain a cone of dimension $2n+1$, $$\iota \colon \tau \hookrightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$$ and the open set $U_\iota$ associated to this map is the intersection of the image of the interior of $\tau$ with the link of $\pi$. The sheaf of integral affine functions has sections $\operatorname{Hom}(\tau,\mathbb{Z})$ on this open set.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-35 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
Definition \ref{defn:IAMSGenKum} specifies a (unique by Lemma~\ref{lem:DataIAMS}) integral affine manifold with singularities $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
The underlying topological space of $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ is canonically the moduli space of $n+1$ points on $B(\mathpzc{A})$ which sum to zero in the group law of $B(\mathpzc{A})$. 
    The singular locus consists of tuples where two or more points meet.
    The underlying topological space of $B^{2n}_K(\mathpzc{A})$ is a manifold (with boundary) by Proposition~\ref{prop:TypeIIHomeotype}. 
    The complement of the singular locus is the closed submanifold of the space of $n+1$ distinct points cut out by the closed condition that points sum to zero. This space inherits an integral affine manifold structure because the differential of the summation map is surjective.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
Making a similar definition for a tropical abelian variety of relative dimension one, yields a space where singularities occur in codimension one. The result is a gadget which could be sensibly described as an integral affine manifold with boundary.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:TypeIHomeotype}
    The link $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ of the generalised Kummer variety is homeomorphic to a simplex of dimension $n$.
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Write $\mathpzc{A} = \mathpzc{A}(\varphi)$. The link of $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\rightarrow \rho$ inherits the topology of $\operatorname{Sym}^{n+1}(B(\varphi))$. Points in the link of $\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\rightarrow \rho$ which specify points summing to $0$ in the group law are precisely the link of $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$. It follows that the underlying topological space of $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ is homeomorphic to the moduli space of $n+1$ points in $S^1$ which sum to zero in the group law on $S^1$. This space is homeomorphic to $\Delta^{n}$ by \cite{Morton_1967} as noted in \cite[Proposition 6.3.4]{BrownMazzon}.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:TypeIIHomeotype}
    The IAMS $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb{CP}^{n}$.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
The argument of Proposition~\ref{prop:TypeIHomeotype} establishes that the link is homeomorphic to the moduli space of $n+1$ points on $(S^1)^2$ which sum to zero. As a topological group, $(S^1)^2$ is isomorphic to the complex points of an (in fact any) elliptic curve $E$. Thus we are required to determine the homeomorphism type of the moduli space of effective degree $n+1$ divisors on an elliptic curve which sum to zero in the group law. But these are precisely the complex sections of a line bundle on $E$ of degree $n+1$ up to rescaling, and thus their moduli is $\mathbb{CP}^n$.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- definition-36: body_md -->
The \textit{collision type} of a point in $B_K^{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ is the unordered tuple of integers $(a_1,...,a_k)$ recording the partition of $n+1$ determined by the multiplicities in the corresponding point of $\text{Sym}^{n+1}(B(\mathpzc{A}/\rho))$.
<!-- end definition-36 -->
<!-- definition-37: body_md -->
\label{defn:TropHilbRn}
    The \textit{tropical Hilbert scheme} $(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n+1]}$ of $n+1$ points on $\mathbb{Z}^s$ is the sheaf on $\textbf{RPC}$ whose $\kappa$ valued points are families of $(n+1)$-weighted zero-dimensional piecewise linear subdivisions of $\mathbb{Z}^s\times \kappa$ over $\kappa$. The \textit{universal tropical subscheme} $\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}(\mathbb{Z}^s)\hookrightarrow \mathbb{Z}^s\times (\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n+1]}$ is defined similarly to $\mathpzc{Z}_{n+1}(\mathpzc{A})$ in Definition \ref{defn:TropHilb}.
<!-- end definition-37 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:TropicalByComponent}
    Let $v$ be a vertex of $B_\Lambda$ of collision type $\textbf{n}(v) = (n_1,...,n_k)$ specifying a ray $\rho_v$ of the cone complex $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$. For some choice of tropical model $$q\colon \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}^\Gamma(\mathbb{Z}^s) \rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s),$$  there is an isomorphism between the star of $\rho_v$ and $\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}^\Gamma(\mathbb{Z}^s)$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:UnivOverComponent}
    The pullback of $\mathpzc{Z}^{\textbf{n}(v)}$ along $q$ is the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_j \Theta_j$ (with the obvious projection map to $\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}^\Gamma(\mathbb{Z}^s)$).
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
We begin by constructing a diagram of sheaves on $\textbf{RPC}_{\text{vert},\rho}$,
    $$
\begin{tikzcd}
\prod_i \underline{(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}} \arrow[r, dashed] \arrow[d,"\Sigma_\mathbb{Z}"] & {\underline{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}} \arrow[d] \\
\underline{\mathbb{Z}}^s \arrow[r] & \underline{\mathpzc{A}}
\end{tikzcd}
$$
The vertical maps are summation in the respective group laws as discussed at the start of Section~\ref{sec:TropGenKummer}. The bottom horizontal map is $w$. Write \textbf{0} for the vertex (i.e. ray but it is a vertex relative base ray) of $\prod_i \underline{(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}}$ which is zero in each factor.

The dashed arrow, which depends on $v$, is defined as follows. 
Note $v$ specifies for each $n_i$ in the collision type a point $x_i$ of $|\mathpzc{A}|$; since the morphism $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\rightarrow \rho$ is saturated, this point comes from a section of $\mathpzc{A}/\rho$.
For each $i$ there is a morphism from a subfunctor of $\underline{(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}}$ (the subfunctor is where the quotient introduces no new collisions) to $\underline{\mathpzc{A}^{[n_i]}}$ defined by $w$ followed by translation by adding $x_i$. 
There is a morphism from a subfunctor of $\prod_i\underline{(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}}$ to $\underline{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}$. 
This is the subfunctor where the quotient introduces no new collisions between points in each factor of $(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}$, and the images of the points associated to different productands $(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}$ do not meet. 
The dashed arrow represents the map defined on this subfunctor. 

The cone complex structure $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$ on $\Sigma_{\operatorname{trop}}^{-1}(\text{id})$ induces a cone complex structure on an open neighbourhood\footnote{This means it induces an equivalence class of cone complex structures about the point which all agree upon restriction to an open set.} of $\textbf{0}$ in $\Sigma_\mathbb{Z}^{-1}({0})$. The dashed arrow is well defined on this open neighbourhood (and the cone complex structure is induced on every open neighbourhood where the dashed arrow is well defined), and induces an isomorphism from the star of the vertex $\textbf{0}$ to the star of the vertex $v$. But the star at the vertex $\textbf{0}$ is a tropical model which we may write $$\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}^\Gamma(\mathbb{Z}^s) \rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s).$$ This proves Lemma \ref{lem:TropicalByComponent}. We deduce Lemma \ref{lem:UnivOverComponent} by applying the same chain of reasoning to the universal tropical subscheme over $\underline{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}$ and $\prod_i \underline{(\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[n_i]}}$ respectively.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- definition-38: body_md -->
