A \emph{semi-abelian scheme} over $S$ is a smooth, separated, commutative group object $G \to S$ in the category of schemes with geometrically connected fibres, such that for each geometric point $s$ in $S$ there exists a short exact sequence of $s$-group schemes
$$
0 \rightarrow T_s \rightarrow G_s = G\times_S s \rightarrow A_s \rightarrow 0
$$
where $T_s \rightarrow s$ is a power of $\mathbb{G}_{m,s}$, and $A_s \to s$ is an abelian scheme.
<!-- end definition-38 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:Summarise Log AV} Let $S$ be an atomic logarithmic scheme with logarithmic structure arising from a map to the Artin cone $a^\ast \sigma$. 
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*]
        \item Every logarithmic abelian variety $A\rightarrow S$ over $S$ is a proper group object in the category of logarithmic S-spaces. Possibly after replacing $S$ by a strict \'etale cover and $A$ by its pullback, there is a canonical commutative square, 
        $$\begin{tikzcd}
A \arrow[r, "\varpi_A"] \arrow[d] & a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(A)= a^\ast \mathpzc{A} \arrow[d] \\
S \arrow[r] & a^\ast \sigma
\end{tikzcd}$$
where horizontal maps are strict, and $\mathsf{Trop}(A)$ is a family of tropical abelian varieties over $\sigma$ (Definition~\ref{defn:TropicalAV}). 
\item The morphism $\varpi_A$ is representable in the category of schemes with logarithmic structure, and the fibre over any map from the standard logarithmic point to $S\times_{a^\ast \sigma} a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(A)$ is a semi-abelian variety. 
        \item Given any tropical model $\Lambda \rightarrow \mathsf{Trop}(A) = \mathpzc{A}$ the composed morphism $$a^\ast \Lambda \times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}} A\rightarrow A \rightarrow  S$$
        is a logarithmically smooth morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure. 
        \item  Let $A\rightarrow \Delta^\circ$ be a family of principally polarised abelian varieties over the generic point of the trait $\Delta$ (see notation section). Then, possibly after replacing $A$ by its base change along a finite map $\Delta\rightarrow \Delta$, there exists a unique polarised logarithmic abelian variety over $\Delta$ extending $A\rightarrow \Delta^\circ$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
Logarithmic abelian varieties are group objects by \cite{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008}, and proper by \cite[Section~11]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartIV}.
The pullback of $A$ to $S_Z$ is a logarithmic abelian variety of constant degeneration \cite[Definition~3.3(1)]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008a}, and is thus the data of a polarisable logarithmic 1-motif\cite[Theorem~3.4]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008a}. 

A polarisable logarithmic 1-motif determines a local system $\textbf{Y}$ of finite rank free $\mathbb{Z}$ modules \cite[Definition~2.2(a)]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008} on $S$, and a semi-abelian variety $G$ over $S$ \cite[Definition~2.2(b)]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008} obtained by extending some abelian variety by a torus $T$. Writing $\textbf{X} = \operatorname{\mathcal{H}om}(T,\mathbb{G}_m)$ the logarithmic 1-motif specifies a pairing \cite[Section 2.3]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008} $$\textbf{Y} \times \textbf{X}
\rightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\sigma,\mathbb{Z}) \text{ or equivalently } \varphi \colon \textbf{Y} \rightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\textbf{X},\operatorname{Hom}(\sigma,\mathbb{Z})).$$ 


Pullback to a point $s$ in $S_Z$ specifies a morphism of $\mathbb{Z}$ modules $$\varphi \colon \textbf{Y} \rightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\textbf{X},\operatorname{Hom}(\sigma,\mathbb{Z})).$$
The isomorphism type is locally constant in $S_Z$ and thus constant because $S$ is atomic which ensures that $S_Z$ is connected. Thus $\varphi$ is well defined independent of the choice of $s$ in $S$. We define $\operatorname{Trop}{A}$ to be $\mathpzc{A}(\varphi)$ in the sense of Definition~\ref{defn:TropicalAV}.

Next we construct the morphism $\varpi_A$.
By definition of logarithmic abelian variety there is a strict \'etale cover $\{S_i\rightarrow S\}$, which we may refine to be a cover by atomic logarithmic schemes, and upon each $S_i$ the $\varpi_A|_{S_i}$ is part of the definition of logarithmic abelian variety: in \cite[Definition~4.1.2]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008a} it is the final non-zero morphism in the displayed sequence of (2).

We have specified morphisms $\varpi_A|_{S_i}$ on the strict \'etale cover $S_i$ of $S$, and it remains to show these morphisms descend to a map from $S$.
Indeed, the map from $A$ to $a^\ast \mathsf{Trop}(A)$ is the stack quotient of $A$ by a subgroup $G$. 
The subgroup $G$ can be characterised as the maximal scheme with logarithmic structure which admits a monomorphism to $A$, has connected fibres over $S$, and is strict over $S$.
Being a subgroup with these properties is stable under strict \'etale pullback upon $S$. The map is thus well defined, and claim (1) is proved.
The short exact sequence of \cite[Definition~4.1.2]{KajiwaraKatoNakayama2008a} insists that fibres over any logarithmic point are isomorphic to the semi-abelian variety $G$. Claim (2) is thus proved.
Claim (3) is \cite[Theorem~8.1, especially Remark(3)]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartIV}, and claim (4) is \cite[Theorem~1.6]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartVII}.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- definition-39: body_md -->
A level $m$ structure on a logarithmic abelian variety $A\rightarrow S$ of dimension $g$ is an isomorphism $$V_S\cong \operatorname{ker}(A\xrightarrow{m} A).$$
<!-- end definition-39 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:commuting square}
    Let $m\geq 3$. There is a commutative diagram with strict horizontal maps which are represented in the category of Noetherian DM stacks with logarithmic structure, $$\begin{tikzcd}
 Y_g(m) \arrow[r, "\widetilde{\varpi}"] \arrow[d, "\pi"'] 
& a^\ast \mathpzc{Y}_g(m) \arrow[d, "a^\ast \pi^{\mathsf{trop}}"] \\
\mathcal A_g(m) \arrow[r, "\varpi"] 
& a^\ast  \mathfrak{A}_g(m)
\end{tikzcd}.$$
Moreover, $\mathcal A_g(m)$ is a proper logarithmic space and the base change of $\mathcal{A}_g(m)$ along any tropical model $\Lambda\rightarrow \mathfrak{A}_g(m)$ is a toroidal compactification of the moduli space of (not logarithmic) abelian varieties.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Note that $\mathcal A_g(m)$ has a model proper over $\mathbb{Z}[1/m]$ which is of finite type over $\mathbb{Z}$ \cite[Theorem~1.7]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartVII}.
    Thus to specify a map from $\mathcal{A}_g(m)$ to $a^\ast \mathfrak{A}_g(m)$ it will suffice to specify the map on functors of points for Noetherian logarithmic schemes. Noetherian logarithmic schemes admit covers by atomic logarithmic schemes \cite[Lemma 2.2.5]{AWbirational}, so it will suffice to specify $\varpi$ on $S$ valued points for $S$ an atomic Noetherian logarithmic scheme. Since $ Y_g(m)$ is proper and thus finite type over $\mathcal A_g(m)$, the same construction can be used to build $\widetilde{\varpi}$.

    We first construct $\varpi$. An $S$ valued point of $\mathcal A_g(m)$ is a logarithmic abelian variety over $S$ equipped with level structure. For $S$ Noetherian and atomic with Artin cone $\varpi_S\colon S\rightarrow a^\ast \sigma$, Proposition~\ref{prop:Summarise Log AV}(1) constructs a family of tropical abelian varieties over $\sigma$. Writing $A^\circ$ for the kernel of $\pi$, $V_S$ for the constant sheaf associated to the module $V\cong (\mathbb{Z}/m\mathbb{Z})^{2g}$ equipped with its standard symplectic form, and composing the level structure with the surjection of Proposition~\ref{prop:Summarise Log AV}(1) yields a surjection $$ \varpi_S^\ast a^\ast V_\sigma \cong V_S\xrightarrow{\sim} A[m]\rightarrow A[m]/A^\circ[m] \cong  \varpi_S^\ast a^\ast \mathpzc{A}[m].$$
    The kernel is coisotropic by \cite[Theorem~9.3(3)]{FeusiLopezTropAV}.
    We thus obtain a morphism from $\sigma$ to $\mathfrak{A}_g(m)$. The map $\varpi$ is the composition $$S \rightarrow a^\ast \sigma \rightarrow a^\ast \mathfrak{A}_g(m).$$ 
    Similarly we obtain the morphism $\widetilde{\varpi}$ from the morphisms of Proposition~\ref{prop:Summarise Log AV}(1).
    
    To see that $\varpi$ is represented in the category of Noetherian DM stacks with logarithmic structure it will suffice to check that for any map from an atomic logarithmic scheme $S\rightarrow a^\ast \mathfrak{A}_g(m) $ the fibre product is an algebraic space with logarithmic structure. Since when $S$ is atomic, the map on tropicalisations corresponds to the map from a cone to $\mathfrak{A}_g$, the claim is demonstrated by the argument of \cite[Section 7.2]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartVII}. The remainder of our theorem concerning representability of the moduli stack and its base changes are restatements of \cite[Theorem~1.6 and Theorem~1.7]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartVII} in the language of this paper.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop:LogAVSmooth}
    Any principally polarised logarithmic abelian surface $g\colon A\rightarrow \Delta_0$ over the standard logarithmic point is polarised smoothable.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
If $A$ is obtained by equipping a conventional abelian surface with strict logarithmic structure over $p$ then the result is clear. Otherwise replace $\Delta_0$ by a logarithmic alteration such that it is possible to choose a basis for the $3$ torsion of $A$. Having done this, we can specify a morphism from $\Delta_0$ to the boundary of $\mathcal{A}_2(3)$. Since the logarithmic structure upon $\Delta_0$ is valuative, this morphism persists after replacing $\mathcal{A}_2(3)$ with a logarithmic modification. We may thus assume that the image of $\Delta_0$ is a point $p$ in the interior (i.e. in a unique boundary divisor) of a boundary divisor in a (representable) logarithmic alteration of $\mathcal{A}_2(3)$. Recall from \cite[Theorem~1.7]{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartVII} that the boundary of a (representable) logarithmic modification of $\mathcal{A}_2(3)$ is toroidal, and thus there exists a map from a trait to $\mathcal{A}_2(3)$ whose generic point does not hit the toroidal boundary, but whose special point is $p$. The universal abelian variety pulls back to the required smoothing $\widetilde{A}$.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- definition-40: body_md -->
A \textit{tropically framed length $n$ closed subscheme of $A_T/T$} is a pair $$(h \colon \Lambda\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}_\tau, \iota\colon Z\hookrightarrow A_T\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}_\tau} a^\ast \Lambda )$$ where:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
    \item The morphism $h$ is a tropical model such that the composed morphism of cone complexes $ \Lambda\rightarrow \tau$ is saturated.
    \item The map $\iota$ is a strict closed immersion of a length $n$ closed subscheme such that the composed map $Z\rightarrow T$ is logarithmically flat.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-40 -->
<!-- definition-41: body_md -->
A \textit{length $n$ closed subscheme of $A_T/T$} is an equivalence class of tropically framed length $n$ closed subscheme of $A_T/T$. The equivalence relation identifies pairs $(h\colon \Lambda \rightarrow \mathpzc{A}_\tau,\iota)$ with $(h'\colon \Lambda'\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}_{\tau},\iota')$ if taking the base change of $\iota$ and $\iota'$ respectively with the projection maps $$A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast \Lambda \leftarrow A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast \Lambda\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast \Lambda'\rightarrow A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}} a^\ast \Lambda'$$ specifies the same closed subscheme. 
    The \textit{logarithmic Hilbert scheme} $A^{[n]}/S$ of length $n$ associated to $A/S$ is the sheafification of the presheaf which assigns to a map $T\rightarrow S$ the set of length $n$ closed subschemes of $A_T/T$.
<!-- end definition-41 -->
<!-- definition-42: body_md -->
A \textit{vertex} of $\Lambda/\tau$ is a cone $v$ of $\Lambda$ such that $|h|$ maps $|v|$ isomorphically to $|\tau|$.
<!-- end definition-42 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:LogHilbProper}
    Continue notation from Proposition~\ref{prop:ModelOfAn}, and fix a choice of $\Lambda$ from the same proposition. Then the morphism $$A^{[m]}_\Lambda := A^{[m]}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}^{[m]}}a^\ast {\mathpzc{A}^{[m]}(\Lambda)}\rightarrow S$$ is a vertical and proper morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure.                                                                                                
       
               
                                                           
                         
             
   
Moreover, $A^{[m]}_\Lambda$ admits an open immersion into the conventional relative Hilbert scheme of points,
$$H^{[m]}_\Lambda := \operatorname{Hilb}^{[m]}\left({A}_{\operatorname{univ}} = \left( A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast\left(\mathpzc{Z}^{[m]}(\Lambda)\right)\right)/S\times_{a^\ast \sigma}a^\ast\mathpzc{A}^{[m]}(\Lambda)\right).$$
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
All of the arguments for this claim are recorded in \cite{LogQuot}, but \textit{op. cit.} is written for a regular crossings pair, so we must note they remain valid in the present situation. The open immersion in the final claim follows from the argument of \cite[Section 6.2]{LogQuot}, and as in \textit{op. cit.} it then follows from \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D01}{0D01}]{stacks} that $A^{[m]}_\Lambda$ is an algebraic stack. This algebraic stack is proper over $S$ by the argument of \cite[Theorem~7.0.1]{LogQuot}. The algebraic stack has finite stabilisers by the argument of \cite[Theorem~8.1.4]{LogQuot}. Vertical holds by construction.
<!-- end proof-22 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{corr:logsmooth}
    The proper model ${A}^{[m]}_\Lambda$  of $A^{[m]}$ is logarithmically smooth over $S$. In particular, $A^{[m]}$ is locally logarithmically smooth over $S$.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-23: body_md -->
Theorem~\ref{thm:LogHilbProper} expresses $A^{[m]}_\Lambda$ as an open subset of the relative Hilbert scheme of points $H^{[m]}_\Lambda$ to a family of surfaces.
Since the map ${A}_{\operatorname{univ}}\rightarrow \operatorname{Exp}:=S\times_{a^\ast \sigma}a^\ast\mathpzc{A}^{[m]}_\Lambda$ 
is logarithmically smooth and strict, it is smooth.\footnote{Note in the definition of $A_{\operatorname{univ}}$ we discarded the non-strict locus - i.e. the singular locus where components meet - when defining our universal expansion.}
By \cite[Theorem~2.9]{Fogarty1968}, $A^{[m]}_\Lambda$ is smooth over $\operatorname{Exp}$, and is thus logarithmically smooth over $S$.
<!-- end proof-23 -->
<!-- lemma-12: body_md -->
\label{lem:LogHCGpMap}
    There are logarithmic Hilbert--Chow ($\mathsf{HC}$) and summation ($\Sigma$) maps
    $${A}^{[m]}\xlongrightarrow{\mathsf{HC}} \mathsf{Sym}^m(A)\xlongrightarrow{\Sigma} {A}.$$
<!-- end lemma-12 -->
<!-- proof-24: body_md -->
Since all spaces involved are noetherian it will suffice to work on $T$ valued points for $T\rightarrow a^\ast \tau$ atomic. The morphism of atomic logarithmic schemes from $T$ to $S$ induces a map $\tau \rightarrow \sigma$ where $a^\ast \sigma$ is the Artin cone of $S$. A morphism from $T$ to $A^{[m]}$ is the data of a closed subscheme of a logarithmic alteration $(T\times_S A)'\rightarrow T\times_S A$ which is logarithmic flat and of length $m$ over $T$. Since the subscheme has relative dimension zero, it must lie in the locus of $(T\times_S A)'$ which is strict over $T$, and is thus flat over $T$. Applying \cite[Paragraph II.3.2]{Iversen1970} we obtain a morphism from the relative Hilbert scheme of $(T\times_S A)'/ T$ to the relative symmetric product of the same morphism. But all sections in the image of the logarithmic Hilbert scheme under this map are strict, so admit a canonical upgrade to sections of the morphism of logarithmic schemes. Thus we have specified a morphism $\mathsf{HC}$ from $T$ to $\operatorname{Sym}^m(A)$ taken in the logarithmic category. 
    The morphism $\Sigma$ is induced from the group structure upon $A$ in the usual way.
<!-- end proof-24 -->
<!-- definition-43: body_md -->
\label{defn:logKummer}
    The logarithmic Kummer variety $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A/S)$ is the fibre product 
$$
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}({A}/S) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & S \arrow[d,"e"] \\
{{A}^{[n+1]}} \arrow[r,"h"]                   & {A}
\end{tikzcd},  
$$
where $e$ is the identity section and $h$ is obtained by composing the morphisms of Lemma \ref{lem:LogHCGpMap}.
<!-- end definition-43 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:ProperLogSmooth}
    Continue notation from Proposition~\ref{prop:KummerSubdivision}, and make a choice of $\Lambda$. The resulting morphism $$\mathrm{Kum}^\Lambda_{2n}({A}/S)\rightarrow S$$
    is a vertical, proper, and logarithmically smooth morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-25: body_md -->
Note that there is a cartesian square,
$$
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(A/S) \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & S \arrow[d] \\
{A^{[n+1]}}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}{a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})} \arrow[r]                   & A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}} a^\ast \sigma
\end{tikzcd},
$$
which we obtain by base change of the diagram in Definition~\ref{defn:logKummer} along compatible morphisms from $a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\rightarrow a^\ast \sigma$ to left and right columns of the associated tropical diagram (see Definition~\ref{defn:TropGenKummer}).
It will thus suffice to establish that the bottom horizontal map, which is the base change of the summation map $h$ of Definition~\ref{defn:logKummer}, is logarithmically smooth. 

The required logarithmic smoothness is equivalent to conventional smoothness of the first morphism, denoted $\Sigma$, in the composition $${A^{[n+1]}}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}}{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})} \xrightarrow{\Sigma}                    A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})}\rightarrow S\times_{a^\ast \sigma}a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}).$$


We begin by establishing flatness of $\Sigma$. Corollary \ref{corr:logsmooth} asserts that the above composition is smooth, and in particular flat. By critère de platitude par fibres \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/039C}{039C}]{stacks}(in the reference using (1) implies (2) direction), flatness of $\Sigma$ may be checked after pulling back along maps from the spectrum of an arbitrary field to $S\times_{a^\ast \sigma}a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$. After such a base change, both domain and codomain of $\Sigma$ are regular since they are (the base change of) spaces which admit a smooth map to a perfect field. Miracle flatness applies to the restriction of $\Sigma$, where the constant fibre has dimension $2n$. 

To complete our proof that $\Sigma$ is smooth, we are left to prove that the fibre of $\Sigma$ over any $\mathbb{C}$ point of $A\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})}$ is smooth\footnote{Since after pullback to a smooth cover which is a scheme we may check upon closed points.}. But for any such fibre there is a semi-abelian variety $A^\circ$ over $\mathbb{C}$ and a tuple of positive integers $n_1,...,n_k$ with sum $n+1$ such that the fibre is isomorphic to the collection of points in $$(A^\circ)^{[n_1]}\times...\times (A^\circ)^{[n_k]}$$ whose sum is $0\in A^\circ$. This locus is smooth by Beauville's original argument for smoothness of generalised Kummer varieties \cite[Section 7, page 769]{Beauville1983}, applied to a semi-abelian variety in place of an abelian variety.
<!-- end proof-25 -->
<!-- definition-44: body_md -->
We say that a morphism of DM stacks with log structure $g\colon X\rightarrow S$ is \textit{locally quasi-projective} if there is a smooth cover $c_i\colon U_i\rightarrow S$ such that $U_i \times_S X\rightarrow U_i$ is a \textit{quasi-projective DM stack} in the sense that it has the following properties.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item $U_i\times_SX$ can be expressed as a global quotient stack of an algebraic space $V_i$ by the action of a subgroup $G$ of $\operatorname{GL}_n/S$ for some integer $n$ where $G$ is flat over $S$. 
        \item $U_i\times_S X$ admits a quasi-projective coarse moduli space.
    \end{enumerate}
    A locally quasi-projective morphism is said to be locally projective if it is also proper.
<!-- end definition-44 -->
<!-- lemma-13: body_md -->
\label{lem:LocProjBaseChange}
    The property of being a locally (quasi)-projective morphism of DM stacks is preserved under base change.
<!-- end lemma-13 -->
<!-- proof-26: body_md -->
We establish the quasi-projective claim: the projective case follows because properness is preserved under base change. The claim follows from two facts. First, by \cite[Example 8.1, Main Properties (3) and Theorem 6.6 (the latter is for uniqueness)]{AlperGoodModuli} passing to a coarse space commutes with base change and the base change of a quasi-projective morphism remains quasi-projective by \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B3G}{0B3G}]{stacks}. Second, being a global quotient stack over $U_i$ is preserved by base change along any map to $U_i$. Flatness of the quotient group scheme, as well as inclusion into the general linear group, are likewise preserved under base change.
<!-- end proof-26 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{prop:Projectivity}
    Let $S$ be a globally charted affine Noetherian logarithmic scheme and let $A\rightarrow S$ be a log abelian variety over $S$. There exist cofinal choices of logarithmic alteration $S'\rightarrow S$ and proper model $A^{[n]}_\Xi\rightarrow A^{[n]}$ which are both saturated and locally projective over $S'$.
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-14: body_md -->
\label{lem:ProjectiveRefinement}
    Let $X$ be a Noetherian log scheme and assume that $X$ has locally free log structure and an Artin fan which is a cone complex. Let $X'\rightarrow X$ be any log alteration. Then there exists a further log alteration $$X''\rightarrow X'\rightarrow X$$ such that the coarse space of $X''$ is projective over $X$.
<!-- end lemma-14 -->
<!-- proof-27: body_md -->
Since $X$ has locally free log structure and admits an Artin fan which is a cone complex, there is an integer $n$ such that the Artin fan of $X$ can be expressed as a Zariski open in the global quotient stack of $\mathbb{A}^n$ by its dense torus. By \cite[Lemma 4.4.7]{logcoh}, we can find $\hat{X}' = X\times_{\mathcal{A}_X}a^\ast \Sigma'$ a log alteration of $X$ where $q_t\colon a^\ast\Sigma'\rightarrow \mathcal{A}_X$ is an alteration.\footnote{The cited lemma is stated only for log modifications but the argument holds also for alterations.} Nothing is lost in assuming that $X' = \hat{X}'$, since we may put ourselves in this situation by replacing $X'$ with a further log alteration. Thus we can arrange that the morphism $q_t$ is obtained by passing to the global quotient stack to an alteration $q'\colon Y'\rightarrow Y$ of toric varieties.

    Every toric alteration can be factored as a root stack followed by a toric modification. By \cite[Example 8.1, Main Properties (3) and Theorem 6.6 (the latter is for uniqueness)]{AlperGoodModuli} we know that passing to the coarse space of a DM stack commutes with fibre products. Therefore Kummer logarithmic alterations are projective. We are thus free to assume that $q_t$ is a logarithmic modification. In summary we have arranged such that $q_t$ is the global quotient stack of a toric modification $q'$. 

    By \cite[Theorem 6.1.18]{CLSToric} (applied to any completion of our fan) the toric modification $q'$ admits a refinement $ Y''\xrightarrow{q''} Y'\xrightarrow{q'} Y$ such that the composition is projective, and thus $Y''$ possesses a line bundle $\mathcal{L}$ which is relatively ample for the composition. Write $\Sigma''$ for the cone complex associated to the Artin fan of $Y''$. By \cite[Section 3.4]{Fulton+2016}, any line bundle on the toric variety $Y''$ is pulled back from a line bundle on the global quotient stack of $Y''$ by its dense torus, and so $\mathcal{L}$ is pulled back from a line bundle $\mathcal{L}_t$ on $a^\ast \Sigma''$. Since the property that a given line bundle is ample may be checked smooth locally on the target \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0D2P}{0D2P}]{stacks}, pulling back $\mathcal{L}_t$ to $X'' = X\times_{\mathcal{A}_X}a^\ast \Sigma''$ specifies a line bundle which is relatively ample over $X$. Since any log alteration is proper, it follows that $X''\rightarrow X$ is proper and the result is proved.
<!-- end proof-27 -->
<!-- proof-28: body_md -->
In this proof we repeatedly saturate maps: when doing so we follow the procedure of \cite{molcho2019universal} (see \cite[1.3.1(2)]{logcoh} for a summary) and thus saturation of a map $Y\rightarrow S'$ proceeds by replacing $S'$ by a logarithmic alteration $S''\to S'$, and replacing $Y$ by $Y\times_{S'}S''$. We will write $\sigma'$ for the subdivision of $\sigma$ such that $S$ admits a strict map to $\sigma'$. In particular, the saturation of a locally projective morphism remains locally projective because the base change of a locally projective map remains locally projective by Lemma \ref{lem:LocProjBaseChange}. 
    We saturate, and thus use this fact, repeatedly. 
    Although this process modifies $S'$, we suppress the change 
    from the notation and continue to write $S'$ for a logarithmic alteration of $S$ 
    whose isomorphism type is repeatedly updated. In making such a modification we lose the ability to assume that $S$ is affine, but may instead assume $S$ is quasi-projective because it is projective over an affine by Lemma~\ref{lem:ProjectiveRefinement}. We similarly abuse notation and do not change notation when replacing other spaces by logarithmic alterations during saturation steps.
    In particular, it will suffice to construct $A^{[n]}_\Xi$ which is projective, but possibly not saturated, over $S'$.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      

    We fix notation which will be used later. Throughout this proof we will discuss quotients of CFGs by the action of a finite group. By this we always mean the stackification of the action groupoid $G \times X \rightrightarrows X$, taken in the strict étale or face topology as dictated by context.

    Since $S$ is globally charted, after saturating ${A}_{\Lambda}\to S'$, the $n$-fold (fs = non fs because our map is saturated) fibre product of ${A}_{\Lambda}$ with itself over $S'$ has Artin fan obtained as the $n$-fold product of $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda$ over $\sigma'$. We denote this Artin fan $(\mathpzc{A}_{\Lambda})^n$. The collision type of points in $(\mathpzc{A}_{\Lambda})^n$ determines a conical (\cite[Section 1.2.1]{LogQuot}), locally 
    closed stratification of $|(\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^n|$. A conical locally closed stratification defines a subdivision of piecewise linear spaces $\mathscr{T}\rightarrow (\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^{n}$, see \cite[Proposition~1.2.5]{LogQuot}. Choose a tropical model 
    $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n} \rightarrow \mathscr{T}$ such that the morphism 
    $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n} \rightarrow  (\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^{n}$ is projective. This is possible: a (possibly not projective) tropical model exists by \cite[Proposition 1.2.5]{LogQuot}, and projective alterations form a co-final system among all choices of logarithmic alteration by Lemma~\ref{lem:ProjectiveRefinement}. 
    
    There is an action of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$ on $\mathpzc{A}^n$ over $\sigma'$ by permuting terms. Without loss of generality, we may assume that $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n}\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^n$ is equivariant for this action. Indeed, given any projective tropical model $\Sigma \to (\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^{n}$, take the common refinement of $w^*(\Sigma)$ 
    over $w \in \operatorname{Sym}(n)$. 
    Projectivity is preserved because the base change of a projective map remains projective. After a further saturation step, we may assume $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n}$ is saturated and projective over $S'$.

    Write $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ for the coarse space of the CFG quotient of 
    $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n}$ by the action of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$; this is a cone space (as defined in \cite{ModStckTropCurve}) by construction, and without loss of generality we may take it to be a cone complex (by subdividing further and using the fact that we constructed our subdivision such that collision type, and thus stabiliser group, is constant on each cone).

    The $n$-fold product $({A}_{\Lambda})^n$ of ${A}_{\Lambda} = {A}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast \mathpzc{A}_{\Lambda}$ with itself over $S'$ is projective over $S'$, being an iterated base change of projective morphisms. The logarithmic alteration
    $$
        {A}_{\Lambda}^n:= ({A}_{\Lambda})^n\times_{a^\ast (\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^{n}}a^\ast \mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n}   \;\rightarrow\; ({A}_{\Lambda})^n,
    $$
    is the base change of a projective morphism $\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{n} \to (\mathpzc{A}_\Lambda)^{n}$, and is thus projective. Since the composition of projective is projective, ${A}_\Lambda^{n}$ is projective over $S$.

    Since automorphisms act by strict morphisms, the CFG quotient of $A_\Lambda^{n}$ by the permutation action of $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$ is represented by 
    a DM stack with logarithmic structure. 
    Write ${A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ for its coarse space, equipped with the descended 
    logarithmic structure (which descends to the stack quotient by definition, and to the coarse space because whenever the group action fixes a scheme theoretic point it also acts trivially on $M_X$). Since 
    ${A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ is the coarse space of a finite quotient of a projective 
    DM stack, it is projective over $S'$ due to the following argument. We may assume the polarising ample is $\operatorname{Sym}(n)$ equivariant by tensoring by its pullbacks along automorphisms, and thus it descends to the quotient stack so that we can apply \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0GFB}{0GFB}]{stacks}.
                                 

    Note that ${A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ admits a strict map to $a^\ast \mathpzc{A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ which itself is a tropical model of $\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}$. Thus ${A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ can be identified with a subset of $\operatorname{Sym}^n(a^\ast\mathpzc{Z}^{[n]}(\Lambda)\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}A/\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}\times_{a^\ast \sigma'}S')$. Combining this observation with Theorem \ref{thm:LogHilbProper}, the conventional Hilbert--Chow map specifies a canonical Hilbert--Chow morphism
    $$
        h \colon {A}_\Lambda^{[n]}:=A^{[n]}\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}^{[n]}}a^\ast\mathpzc{A}^{(n)}_\Lambda \;\longrightarrow\; {A}_\Lambda^{(n)}.
    $$
    We already know that ${A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ is locally projective, so will check that the above morphism is projective. By \cite[Corollaire 9.6.4]{EGA5}, 
    it is enough to exhibit a line bundle on $\overline{A}_\Lambda^{[n]}$ whose restriction to fibres over $\overline{A}_\Lambda^{(n)}$ is ample. The morphism we are required to show projectivity of is precisely the relative Hilbert--Chow morphism associated to the relative Hilbert scheme of points for the morphism $A_{\operatorname{univ}}\rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n]}$. Writing $p\colon Z_n\rightarrow A^{[n]}$ for the universal subscheme and $L$ for the pullback of the ample on $A_\Lambda$ to $Z_n$, the line bundle $\operatorname{det}(p_\ast L)$ is ample on fibres of the above Hilbert Chow map, because it restricts to the Pl\"ucker bundle (with respect to any choice of ample on an alteration of $A$) on fibres of $h$.
<!-- end proof-28 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{corr:projectivityGenKummer}
    Let $A\rightarrow S$ be a logarithmic abelian variety over $S$ an atomic scheme with logarithmic structure. There is a locally projective, vertical, logarithmically smooth, and saturated morphism $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(A)\rightarrow S'$$ which fits into a commutative square with two sides logarithmic alterations and the final side the morphism $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)\rightarrow S$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-29: body_md -->
Writing $\mathpzc{A}\rightarrow \sigma$ for the associated family of tropical abelian varieties, choose a tropical alteration $\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}_\Lambda \rightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n]}$ such that the subsheaf $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}):= \mathpzc{A}^{[n]}_\Lambda\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}} \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}) \hookrightarrow \mathpzc{A}^{[n]}_\Lambda$$ is the inclusion of a sub-cone complex. By the cofinality statement of Proposition \ref{prop:Projectivity} we are free to assume that $\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}_\Lambda\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n]}} A$ is locally projective over some logarithmic alteration $S'$ of $S$. Thus $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(A)$ is a strict closed subscheme of a locally projective, vertical, and saturated logarithmic scheme over $S'$, and is thus locally projective over $S'$. Logarithmic smoothness is Proposition~\ref{prop:ProperLogSmooth}.
<!-- end proof-29 -->
<!-- proposition-13: body_md -->
\label{prop:TwoFormExist}
    Let $A\rightarrow \Delta_0$ be a principally polarised logarithmic abelian surface, and write $\mathsf{pr}_i\colon A^{n+1}\rightarrow A$ for the $i^\text{th}$ projection map. 
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item There is a unique (up to scaling) section $\eta_A$ of $\omega^2_{A/\Delta_0}$.
        \item The form $\sum_i \mathsf{pr}^\ast_i \eta_A$ on $A^{n+1}$ descends to a 2-form ${\eta}_\circ^{(n+1)}$ on the complement of the large diagonal in $A^{(n+1)}$. Identifying the complement of the large diagonal of $A^{(n+1)}$ with the complement of the Hilbert--Chow exceptional divisor in $A^{[n+1]}$, this form extends uniquely to a global section ${\eta}^{[n+1]}$ of $\omega^2_{A^{[n+1]}/\Delta_0}$.
    \end{enumerate}
   We write $\eta$ for the pullback of $\eta^{[n+1]}$ to $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)$ under the inclusion $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)\hookrightarrow A^{[n+1]}.$$ 
    \begin{enumerate}[start = 3, leftmargin = *]
        \item The form $\eta$ is \textit{nowhere degenerate}, in that it induces an isomorphism
    $$\phi_\eta\colon \mathsf{T}_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0}^\mathsf{log}\rightarrow \omega^1_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0}\quad \quad  v \mapsto \eta(v,-).$$
    \item There is an equality, $$H^0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\omega^2_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0}) = \mathbb{C} \eta.$$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-13 -->
<!-- lemma-15: body_md -->
\label{lem:ExtendSections}
    Let $X\rightarrow \Delta$ be a logarithmically smooth integral morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item Then both $X$ and $X_0 \cong X\times_\Delta \Delta_0$ are Cohen--Macaulay (CM).
        \item Let $\mathcal{E}$ be any vector bundle on $X_0$ (resp. $X$) and let $j\colon U\hookrightarrow X_0$ be an open subscheme of $X_0$ (resp $X$) whose complement has codimension at least two in $X_0$ (resp. $X$). Then the morphism $\mathcal{E}\rightarrow j_\ast j^\ast \mathcal{E}$ is an isomorphism. In particular, any section of $\mathcal{E}|_{U}$ extends to a section of $\mathcal{E}$.
        \item Let $Y$ be any smooth scheme, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be any vector bundle on $Y$. Let $j'\colon W\subset Y$ be an open subset whose complement has codimension at least two. Then the morphism $\mathcal{E}\rightarrow j'_\ast (j')^\ast \mathcal{E}$ is an isomorphism, and in particular every section of $\mathcal{E}|_W$ extends to a section of $\mathcal{E}$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-15 -->
<!-- proof-30: body_md -->
Note that $\Delta$ is CM because it is the spectrum of a regular local ring. The morphism from $X$ to $\Delta$ is logarithmically smooth and integral, and is thus a CM map. It follows that $X$ is CM. 
    We know that $X_0$ is CM by the final sentence of \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02JN}{02JN}]{stacks}. Thus (1) is proved.

    To establish (2) we would like to apply \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E9I}{0E9I}]{stacks}. Cohen-Macaulay ensures that every point of codimension at least two in $X_0$ also has depth at least two, and thus $\mathcal{E}$ has depth two at every point of the codimension at least two locus $X\backslash U$. All except the final sentence is an \'etale local claim, so the scheme hypothesis does no harm. The final sentence follows by definition of pushforward.

    Claim (3) follows similarly - using the fact that any smooth scheme is CM.
<!-- end proof-30 -->
<!-- proof-31: body_md -->
We first prove claim (1). By \cite[Theorem~2.6]{FujisawaNakayama2020} the logarithmic Hodge numbers of $A$ coincide with the Hodge numbers of the conventional abelian surface which is the general fibre of $\widetilde{A}/\Delta$. Appealing to \cite[Proposition 7.27]{EGM-AV} for these conventional Hodge numbers, we deduce that $h^{0,2}_{\log}(A/\Delta_0)=1$ completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-31 -->
<!-- proof-32: body_md -->
The first sentence of (2) is strict \'etale descent and we will now prove the rest of (2). 
    Our proof requires the following construction. 
    By Proposition~\ref{prop:LogAVSmooth} we can find a logarithmic abelian variety $\widetilde{\pi}\colon \widetilde{A}\rightarrow \Delta$ whose special fibre is $A$. We write $\widetilde{\pi}_{[n+1]}\colon \widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}\rightarrow \Delta$ for the relative Hilbert scheme.
    
    Let $U_2^{[n+1]}$ be the open subset of some logarithmic alteration $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}_\Xi\rightarrow \widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}$ which is disjoint from the exceptional divisor of the Hilbert--Chow map and let $U_1^{[n+1]} = \widetilde{\pi}^{-1}(\Delta \backslash\Delta_0)$. 
    The form $\eta_\circ^{[n+1]}|_{U_1^{[n+1]}\cap U_2^{[n+1]}}$ extends from $U_1^{[n+1]}\cap U_2^{[n+1]}$ to $U_1^{[n+1]}$ by the smooth case proved by Beauville in \cite{Beauville1983}. 
    By the argument of the first sentence of the previous paragraph, $\eta_\circ^{[n+1]}|_{U_1^{[n+1]}\cap U_2^{[n+1]}}$ extends to a form on $U_2^{[n+1]}$. 
    By Zariski descent the previous two sentences give us an extension $\eta_{12}$ of $\eta_\circ^{[n+1]}|_{U_2^{[n+1]}}$ to $U_1^{[n+1]}\cup U_2^{[n+1]}$. Note $\omega^2_{A^{[n]}/\Delta_0}$ is locally free because $A^{[n]}$ is log \'etale locally logarithmically smooth by Corollary~\ref{corr:logsmooth}, so without loss of generality $\omega^2_{A^{[n]_\Xi}/\Delta_0}$ is strict \'etale locally smooth. 
    
    We claim that the codimension of the complement of $U_2^{[n+1]}\cap \widetilde{\pi}_{[n]}^{-1}(0)$ is at least one within $\widetilde{\pi}_{[n]}^{-1}(0)$. Indeed, each irreducible component of $\widetilde{\pi}_{[n]}^{-1}(0)$ contains a dense open which is a conventional Hilbert scheme of points on a smooth (but not compact) surface. The complement of the locus where no two points meet is codimension one in any such Hilbert scheme. 
    
    Since $\widetilde{\pi}_{[n]}^{-1}(0)$ is itself codimension one, we deduce that the complement of $U_1^{[n+1]}\cup U_2^{[n+1]}$ is codimension two in the total space of $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}_\Xi$.
    It follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:ExtendSections}(2) (total space case) that $\eta_{12}$ extends to a form on $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}_\Xi$ and (2) is proved.
<!-- end proof-32 -->
<!-- proof-33: body_md -->
Choose a tropical model $\widetilde{A}^n_\Xi\rightarrow \widetilde{A}^n$ saturated over $\Delta$ such that there exists a logarithmic alteration $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Xi(\widetilde{A})\rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\widetilde{A})$ for which there is a strict map $f\colon \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Xi(\widetilde{A})\rightarrow \widetilde{A}^{(n)}_\Xi$. Since the tropicalisations of $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}$ and $\widetilde{A}^{(n+1)}$ coincide, we obtain a logarithmic alteration of $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}_\Xi$ of $\widetilde{A}^{[n+1]}$ from this data.  Let $U_1,U_2$ be the preimages of $U_1^{[n+1]},U_2^{[n+1]}$ respectively under $f$.
    We will show that the restriction of $\phi_\eta$ to the union of $U_1$ and $U_2$ is an isomorphism. Since hom sheaves of vector bundles are themselves hom sheaves, the result will follow from Lemma \ref{lem:ExtendSections}(2). 
    
    Restricting to $U_1$ we are in the non-logarithmic situation, and the result is true by \cite{Beauville1983}. To establish the result on $U_2$, note that checking $\phi_\eta$ is an isomorphism can be done on stalks. By \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00DV}{00DV}]{stacks} it is enough that the morphism pulls back to an isomorphism on the fibres over closed points. It will suffice to check that the pullback to the special fibre $U_2^{0} = \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Xi(A/\Delta_0)\cap U_2$ is an isomorphism.

    Fix a point $p$ in $U_2^0$ whose image in $A^{(n)}$ is $\overline{p}$. Let $q$ in $A^{n+1}$ be a preimage of $\overline{p}$ under the quotient map. Note by construction $q$ is disjoint from the large diagonal. The two form on $A$ is dual to coordinates $x,y$ on the stalk of $T_A$ at the point $\mathsf{pr}_i(q)$. Pulling back along $\mathsf{pr}_i$ for all $i$ yields a natural set of coordinates $x_i,y_i$ for $A^{n+1}$ about $q$. Since $q$ lies in $U_2$, the quotient map is \'etale and these coordinates descend to a set of coordinates $x_i,y_i$ about ${p}$.

     The form $\eta^{(n+1)}$ can now be expressed in the dual basis as $dx_i\wedge dy_i$. We highlight that $d x_i$ and $dy_i$ need not be of the form $df$ for $f$ in $\mathcal{O}_X$ or $M_X$, and will in general be a sum of such terms. Write $B_2$ for the matrix representing $dx \wedge dy$ with respect to the basis $(x,y)$. The restriction of $\eta$ to the tangent bundle of $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)$ is represented by the restriction of the matrix $\mathsf{Diag}(B_2,....,B_2)$ to the subspace where all even and all odd coordinates add to zero. By elementary linear algebra, the matrix is non-degenerate, and thus neither is $\eta$.
<!-- end proof-33 -->
<!-- proof-34: body_md -->
We have shown that $C\eta \leq H^0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\omega^2_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0})$ with $\eta$ non-degenerate. It remains to show that $h^0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\omega^2_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0})=1$.
                                                                                                                                                                                
     Indeed, writing $K_{(2n)}(A)$ for the preimage of $0$ under the summation map $A^{(n+1)}\rightarrow A$, there is a restricted Hilbert--Chow morphism $\operatorname{HC}\colon \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)\rightarrow K_{(2n)}(A)$. For every choice of model $K_{(2n)}^\Xi\rightarrow K_{(2n)}$, the morphism of logarithmic alterations $$\operatorname{HC}_{\Xi}\colon \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Xi(A)\rightarrow K_{(2n)}^\Xi(A)$$ is an isomorphism on dense open subsets whose complement in $K_{(2n)}^\Xi$ we denote $W$. Note $W$ is the locus where two or more points meet, and thus has codimension two.  
     Thus we have an injection $$H^0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\omega^2_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)/\Delta_0})\hookrightarrow H^0(\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}^\Xi(A)\backslash W,\omega^2_{\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A)/\Delta_0})$$ and it will suffice to show that $h^0(K_{(2n)}^\Xi\backslash W,\omega^2_{\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A)/\Delta_0})=1$ for some choice of $\Xi$.

     To complete the proof of (4) consider the morphism 
     $$R\colon A^{n}\rightarrow \operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A)$$ 
     $$(a_1,...,a_n)\mapsto \left[\left(a_1,...,a_n,-\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\right)\right].$$ 
     Note $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ acts on the domain via the embedding $A^n\rightarrow A^{n+1}$ which induces $R$. We can choose $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ equivariant logarithmic alterations with domains which are DM stacks with logarithmic structure, $$A^{n+1}_{\Xi}\rightarrow A^{n+1}\text{ and }A^{n}_{\Xi}\rightarrow A^n\times_{A^{n+1}}A^{n+1}_\Xi.$$ We can assume that the latter is saturated because universal semistable reducition preserves $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ symmetry. The image of the latter map lies within $K^\Xi_{(2n)}$ for the induced choice of $\Xi$. Thus we obtain a morphism of DM stacks with logarithmic structure $$R_\Xi\colon A^{n}_\Xi \rightarrow \operatorname{K}_{(2n)}^\Xi.$$
     The map $R_\Xi$ is a $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ torsor away from $$R_\Xi^{-1}(W) = \left \{ (a_1,...,a_n)|a_i=a_j\text{ some } i,j\right\} \cup \left\{(a_1,...,a_n) \text{ such that }\exists j\text{ with } a_j = -\sum_{i=1}^n a_i\right\}.$$

    We deduce that the restriction of $R_\Xi$ to the complement of $R_\Xi^{-1}(W)$ is the global quotient stack of $A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)$ by the free action of the symmetric group on $n+1$ letters. 
    The map $R|_{A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)}$ is strict and \'etale so $\omega^2_{\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A)/\Delta_0}$ pulls back along the quotient map to $\omega^2_{A^n/\Delta_0}|_{A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)}$. 
    The proof of (4) will be complete when we show the final equality in the chain $$h^0(\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A),\omega^2_{\operatorname{K}_{(2n)}(A)/\Delta_0}) = \operatorname{dim}(H^0(A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W),\omega^2_{A^n/\Delta_0}|_{A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)})^{\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)}) = 1$$
    
    Since $W$ is codimension at least two and $R_\Xi$ is finite, the inclusion of $A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)\hookrightarrow A^n_\Xi$ is an isomorphism outside a locus of codimension at least two. 
    Lemma \ref{lem:ExtendSections}(2) applies and we deduce that pullback induces an isomorphism which respects the symmetric group action, $$H^0(A^n\backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W),\omega^2_{A^n/\Delta_0}|_{A^n_\Xi \backslash R_\Xi^{-1}(W)}) \cong H^0(A^n,\omega^2_{A^n/\Delta_0}).$$ It remains to show that the vector bundle $\omega^2_{A^n/\Delta_0}$ on $A^n$ admits a single dimension of symmetric group invariant sections. 
    
    Letting $\widetilde{A}/\Delta$ be a logarithmic abelian variety with central fibre $A/\Delta_0$, note that by the main results of \cite{KajiwaraKatoNakayamaPartIV} $\widetilde{A}$ admits a logarithmic alteration which is a scheme with logarithmic structure. It follows from \cite{FujisawaNakayama2020} that the logarithmic Hodge theory of $A$ specifies a variation of logarithmic Hodge structure on $\Delta$. Thus the logarithmic Hodge numbers of any logarithmic abelian surface coincide with the logarithmic Hodge numbers of a smooth abelian surface, and we deduce that $h^0(A,\omega^1) =2.$ Choose generators $\langle x^a,x^b\rangle \cong H^0(A,\omega^1)$ for this group. Since $\omega^1$ is additive over direct products, we obtain a basis $$H^0(\omega^1,A^n) = \langle x_1^a = p_1^\ast x^a,x_1^b = p_1^\ast x^b,..., x_n^b = p_n^\ast x^b \rangle.$$
    Note that by \cite[Chapter VI, Theorem 1.1(3)]{FaltingsChai1990} $\omega^1$ is the trivial rank two vector bundle: thus taking wedge power commutes with global sections. 
    
    Thus $H^0(\omega^2,A^n)$ has dimension $2n$ choose $2$. We now describe its structure as a $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ representation. Following \cite[Proposition 3.12]{FultonHarris}, the canonical representation of $\operatorname{Sym}(n+1)$ on a vector space with basis indexed by $1,...,n+1$ splits as the direct sum $\operatorname{trivial}\oplus \operatorname{Std}$ where $\operatorname{Std}$ is irreducible by \cite[Proposition 3.12]{FultonHarris}. Certainly there is an isomorphism of representations $$H^0(\omega^2,A^n)\cong \left(\operatorname{Std}\oplus \operatorname{Std}\right) \bigwedge \left(\operatorname{Std}\oplus \operatorname{Std}\right)\cong \left(\operatorname{Std}\wedge\operatorname{Std}\right)^{\oplus 2}\oplus \operatorname{Std}\otimes \operatorname{Std}.$$ By \cite[Proposition 3.12]{FultonHarris} $\operatorname{Std}\wedge\operatorname{Std}$ is irreducible but not the trivial irreducible representation. By \cite[Comment end of section 3.2]{FultonHarris} $\operatorname{Std}\otimes \operatorname{Std}$ has at least a one dimensional space of invariants, and by \cite[Proposition 2.1]{FultonHarris} $\operatorname{Std}$ being a real irreducible representation is self dual so in fact the $G$-invariant part of $\operatorname{Std}\otimes \operatorname{Std}\cong \operatorname{Std}\otimes \operatorname{Std}^\vee \cong \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Std},\operatorname{Std})$ has dimension at most one by Schur's lemma completing the proof.
<!-- end proof-34 -->
<!-- lemma-16: body_md -->
\label{lem:LogSimplyConnected}
    Let $A\rightarrow \Delta_0$ be a principally polarised logarithmic abelian surface. There are isomorphisms
        $$\pi_1(\mathsf{KN}_0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A/\Delta_0)))\cong \operatorname{ker}(\pi_1^{\operatorname{log}}(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A/\Delta_0))\rightarrow \pi_1^{\operatorname{log}}(\Delta_0))\cong 0.$$
<!-- end lemma-16 -->
<!-- proof-35: body_md -->
The first isomorphism is a definition. For the second isomorphism note that by Proposition~\ref{prop:LogAVSmooth} and Proposition~\ref{prop:ProperLogSmooth} there is a logarithmically smooth morphism $$\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\widetilde{A})\rightarrow \Delta$$ which has central fibre which is a logarithmic alteration of the generalised Kummer variety in the lemma's statement. The general fibre has trivial fundamental group by \cite{Beauville1983}, and thus by Lemma~\ref{lem:Serre Fibration} we deduce that after replacing $A/\Delta_0$ by a kummer logarithmic alteration pulled back from $\Delta$ we have $\pi_1(\mathsf{KN}_0(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A/\Delta_0)))\cong 0$. But the statement descends along a kummer logarithmic alteration pulled back from $\Delta$: such an alteration only replaces $\operatorname{KN}(\Delta_0)\cong S^1$ by a finite covering space. Pulling back along a covering space does not affect homotopy groups of the fibres.
<!-- end proof-35 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
\label{corr:familyIHS}
    Let $A\rightarrow S$ be a principally polarised family of logarithmic abelian surfaces. The associated generalised Kummer variety $\pi\colon \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A)\rightarrow S$ is a family of logarithmic IHS varieties.
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
<!-- proof-36: body_md -->
We verify that the hypotheses of Definition~\ref{defn:LogIHS} hold. Proposition~\ref{prop:ProperLogSmooth} ensures that $\pi$ is logarithmically smooth and proper over $S$. Relatively simply connected is Lemma~\ref{lem:LogSimplyConnected}. The logarithmic symplectic structure is recorded in Proposition~\ref{prop:TwoFormExist}. Corollary \ref{corr:projectivityGenKummer} ensures after base change to any standard log point there is a projective logarithmic modification.
<!-- end proof-36 -->
<!-- situation-1: body_md -->
\label{sitch}
Set $A\rightarrow \Delta$ be a family of logarithmic abelian surfaces, and write $\mathcal{X}' = \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}({A})/\Delta$ for the associated logarithmic generalised Kummer variety. Choosing a tropical model with domain a free cone complex and saturating the resulting morphism \cite{AbramovichKaru,molcho2019universal} specifies a saturated map $\pi \colon \mathcal{X}/\Delta$ of DM stacks with logarithmic structure. There is a corresponding saturated morphism of cone complexes $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}) \rightarrow \rho$ where $\rho$ is a ray, $a^\ast \rho$ is the Artin fan of $\Delta$, and $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}) \rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})$ is a tropical model.
<!-- end situation-1 -->
<!-- lemma-17: body_md -->
The cokernel of the map $\mathbb{G}_m\hookrightarrow \mathbb{G}_m^\text{log}$ is the sheaf $\mathbb{G}_m^\text{trop}:= a^\ast \mathbb{Z}$.
<!-- end lemma-17 -->
<!-- proof-37: body_md -->
The cokernel has functor of points obtained by sheafifying the presheaf which sends a test scheme $T$ to $\Gamma(T,\overline{M}_T^{\operatorname{gp}})$. On the other hand, the functor of points of $a^\ast \mathbb{Z}$ is obtained by sheafifying the presheaf which sends a test scheme $T$ to the collection of maps from $\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{M}_T,\mathbb{N})$ to $\mathbb{Z}$. There is an isomorphism of monoids $$\overline{M}_T^{\operatorname{gp}}\rightarrow \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{M}_T,\mathbb{N}),\mathbb{Z}).$$ To see that this map is an isomorphism note first that by duality for fine and saturated torsion-free monoids $\overline{M}_T\cong \operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{Hom}(\overline{M}_T,\mathbb{N}),\mathbb{N})$; and note second that for any toric monoid $A$ there is an equality $\operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb{Z}) = \operatorname{Hom}(A,\mathbb{N})^{\operatorname{gp}}$.
<!-- end proof-37 -->
<!-- definition-45: body_md -->
\label{defn:Alog}
    Let $A^\circ$ be a semi-abelian variety, and write $\mathbb{G}_m^s$ for the 
    \textit{torus part of $A^{\circ}$}, i.e. the kernel of the map from $A^\circ$ to its Albanese. We write 
    $$A^\text{log} = [A^\circ\times (\mathbb{G}^\text{log}_m)^s/\mathbb{G}_m^s]$$
    where $\mathbb{G}_m^s$ acts diagonally as the subtorus of the second factor, and as the torus part of $A^\circ$.
<!-- end definition-45 -->
<!-- definition-46: body_md -->
The \textit{logarithmic Hilbert scheme} $(A^{\log})^{[m]}$ of $m$ points on $A^\text{log}$ is defined through its functor of points on the category of fine and saturated logarithmic schemes, which assigns to a test scheme $S$ the set of equivalence classes of pairs $$(Y'\rightarrow S\times A^\mathsf{log}, Z'\hookrightarrow Y'),$$ 
    where:
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item The scheme with logarithmic structure $Y'$ is a logarithmic alteration of $S\times A^\mathsf{log}$ which is saturated over $S$. 
        \item The morphism $Z'\hookrightarrow Y'$ is a strict closed immersion of Hilbert polynomial $m$ which renders $Z'$ logarithmically flat over $S$.
        \item The equivalence relation identifies $(Y',Z'\hookrightarrow Y')$ with $(Y'',Z''\hookrightarrow Y'')$ if the pullbacks of $Z'$ and $Z''$ to $Y''\times_{S\times A^\mathsf{log}} Y'$ coincide.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-46 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:ComponentlogHilb}
    There is a strict morphism represented by DM stacks with logarithmic structure $$(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[m]}\rightarrow a^\ast (\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[m]}.$$
    Moreover for any choice of tropical model $$ (\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[m]}(\Lambda)\rightarrow (\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[m]},$$ there is a canonical open immersion into a (conventional) relative Hilbert scheme, $$(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[m]}(\Lambda) \rightarrow {\operatorname{Hilb}}^m(A^{\operatorname{log}} \times_{a^\ast\mathbb{Z}^s}a^\ast \mathpzc{Z}_{m}(\mathbb{Z}^{s})(\Lambda) /a^\ast (\mathbb{Z}^s)^{[m]}(\Lambda)).$$
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-38: body_md -->
The arguments of \cite{LogQuot} apply as written to this more general situation.
<!-- end proof-38 -->
<!-- definition-47: body_md -->
Writing $\iota_0$ for the inclusion of the identity into the group $A^\circ$ (which we identify with a subgroup of $A^{\log}$), we define two further variants of the logarithmic Kummer variety: $$
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)
  \arrow[r]
  \arrow[d]
&
\displaystyle \prod_{n_i \in \mathbf{n}(v)} (A^\circ)^{[n_i]}
  \arrow[d,"m"]
\\
\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{C})
  \arrow[r,"\iota_0"]
&
A^\circ
\end{tikzcd}
\quad \quad
\begin{tikzcd}
\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^{\log})
  \arrow[r]
  \arrow[d]
&
\displaystyle \prod_{n_i \in \mathbf{n}(v)} (A^{\log})^{[n_i]}
  \arrow[d,"m"]
\\
\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{C})
  \arrow[r,"\iota_0"]
&
A^{\log}
\end{tikzcd}.
$$
<!-- end definition-47 -->
<!-- definition-48: body_md -->
Let $\Sigma$ be a cone complex and let $\kappa$ be a cone in $\Sigma$. Consider a morphism of algebraic stacks $$X\rightarrow a^\ast \Sigma.$$ Note that there is an open immersion of the stack quotient of the toric variety associated to $\kappa$ by its dense torus into $a^\ast \Sigma$. Write $W_\kappa$ for the image of the closed torus orbit under the stack quotient followed by open immersion. The \textit{stratum of $X$ associated to $\kappa$} is $X\times_{a^\ast \Sigma}W_\kappa$.
<!-- end definition-48 -->
<!-- proposition-14: body_md -->
\label{prop:KummerStrataIrreducible}Let $$\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)\rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$$ be any tropical model. Define $$\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}}) = \operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)\times_{ \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)} \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}}).$$
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin =*]
        \item The stack $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$ is represented by an irreducible smooth scheme of dimension $2n$.
        \item The canonical inclusion $$\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)\hookrightarrow \operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$$ is the inclusion of a dense open into a logarithmically smooth DM stack with logarithmic structure.
        \item For any cone $\kappa$ in the cone complex $\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$, the stratum of $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ associated to $\kappa$ is irreducible.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-14 -->
<!-- proof-39: body_md -->
We first prove (1). 
    $(A^\circ)^{[n_i]}$ is a conventional Hilbert scheme of points on a smooth surface and is thus a smooth scheme. The morphism $m$ is smooth by the argument of \cite[Second paragraph of Section 7]{Beauville1983} - which applies to semi-abelian varieties just as well as to abelian varieties. Since smoothness is preserved under base change and since also the category of schemes is closed under fibre products, $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$ is a smooth scheme. 
    A connected DM stack which is smooth over a field is irreducible by \cite[Lemma 4.5]{shi2026gcompanionsalgebraicstacksapplications}. 
    It remains to argue that $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$ is connected. 
    Indeed, let $$K_{(\textbf{n}(v))}(A^\circ) = \left(\prod_i\operatorname{Sym}^{n_i}(A^\circ)\right)\times_{A^\circ} e$$ where the product is over the product map and the inclusion $e\rightarrow A^\circ$ of the identity.
    The Hilbert--Chow map restricts to define a universally closed morphism $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)\rightarrow K_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$, and this morphism is surjective. Since fibres of the Hilbert--Chow map are connected, by \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0377}{0377}]{stacks} it suffices to show that $K_{\mathbf{n}(v)}$ is connected. 
    But $(A^\circ)^n$ is connected, and there is a surjective map $(A^\circ)^n\rightarrow K_{\mathbf{n}(v)}$ sending $(a_1,...,a_n)$ to $(a_1,...,a_n, -\sum_ia_i)$. 
    Since the image of a connected set is connected, the result is proved.

    We now prove (2). Note that $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ is a DM stack with logarithmic structure by argument of Proposition \ref{prop:ProperLogSmooth} - i.e. it is an open subset in the conventional relative Hilbert scheme of Theorem \ref{thm:ComponentlogHilb}. Logarithmic smoothness is also similar to Proposition \ref{prop:ProperLogSmooth}. Logarithmic smoothness ensures that the map from $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ to $a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$ is smooth, and thus flat of finite presentation. A flat morphism of finite presentation is open, and thus the preimage of any dense set in $a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$ is dense in $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$. But $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$ is the preimage of the dense set $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb{C})\subset a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$. Thus $\operatorname{Kum}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)$ is dense in $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$.

    Finally we prove (3). By (2) we know that $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ is logarithmically smooth. Therefore the stratum of $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ associated to $\kappa$, being a fibre over the (smooth) map to the Artin fan, is smooth. Again by \cite[Lemma 4.5]{shi2026gcompanionsalgebraicstacksapplications}, it will suffice to check that the stratum associated to $\kappa$ is connected. 
    
    Writing $\textbf{n}_\kappa(v)$ for the collision type specified by any point in the interior of $\kappa$, the stratum associated to $\kappa$ is the stack quotient of $\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}_\kappa(v)}(A^\circ)$ by the action of a group. But we already argued that schemes of the form $\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}_\kappa(v)}(A^\circ)$ are connected, and the image of a connected set is connected. The result is proved.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- definition-49: body_md -->
For $v$ any vertex of $B_\Lambda$ let $\mathcal{X}_v^0$ be the fibre product, 
$$
\begin{tikzcd}
\mathcal{X}_v^0 \arrow[r] \arrow[d] & Y_v \arrow[d, hook] \\
\mathcal{X}_0 \arrow[r] & E.
\end{tikzcd}
$$
<!-- end definition-49 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:ExplicitDescription} We establish the following statements.
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
    \item The morphism $$\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}\hookrightarrow \underline{\mathcal{X}_0}$$ is the inclusion of an irreducible component. 
    \item For some choice of tropical model 
    $\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)\rightarrow \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$ there is an isomorphism in the category of algebraic stacks between $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$ and $\underline{\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}^\Gamma(A^{\operatorname{log}})}$.
    \item There is an isomorphism in the category of algebraic stacks between $\underline{\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^\circ)}$ and the interior\footnote{That is, the open subset disjoint from all other components.} of $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$. 
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
Note (3) follows directly from (2) by restricting attention to the open where the logarithmic structure has minimal rank. Next we show that (1) also follows once claim (2) is established. Indeed, first observe that $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$, being the preimage of an irreducible component under the tropicalisation map, is closed in $\underline{\mathcal{X}_0}$. Also $\underline{\mathcal{X}_0}$ is the union over $v$ of the $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$. By combining (2) with Proposition \ref{prop:KummerStrataIrreducible}, we learn that each $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$ is irreducible of dimension $2n$, so no one $\underline{\mathcal{X}_v^0}$ is properly contained in another. It remains to prove claim (2).
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- lemma-18: body_md -->
\label{lem:StarAsComponent}
        There is an isomorphism in the category of algebraic stacks $$\underline{Y_v}\cong \underline{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)}.$$
<!-- end lemma-18 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
By Lemma \ref{lem:TropicalByComponent} it will suffice to identify $\underline{Y_v}$ with $\underline{a^\ast\operatorname{Star}_{\rho_v}( \operatorname{Kum}^\Lambda_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}))}$.
        Note $\underline{Y_v}$ has a Zariski cover $U_\sigma \rightarrow \underline{Y_v}$ indexed by cones $\sigma$ of $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$ which contain $\sigma$ as a face. Indeed, this cover is pulled back from the open cover of $\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$ indexed by the toric dictionary. By definition of star,  $\underline{a^\ast\operatorname{Star}_{\rho_v}( \operatorname{Kum}^\Lambda_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}))}$ has a Zariski open cover $$V_\sigma \rightarrow \underline{a^\ast\operatorname{Star}_{\rho_v}( \operatorname{Kum}^\Lambda_{2n}(\mathpzc{A}))}$$ with the same indexing set. 

        The proof will be complete if we provide for each $\sigma$ an isomorphism $V_\sigma\cong U_\sigma$ in a fashion compatible with face maps.
        We fix $\sigma$ and construct the desired isomorphism. Let $X_\sigma$ be the toric variety associated to $\sigma$ so that $a^\ast \sigma = [X_\sigma/X_\sigma^\circ]$. 
        Write $h\colon \sigma^{\operatorname{gp}}\rightarrow \mathbb{Z} = \rho^{\operatorname{gp}}$ for the lattice map induced by $\sigma \rightarrow \rho.$ Letting $u_v$ be the primitive generator of $\rho_v$, saturation means that projection induces an isomorphism
$$
g\colon \operatorname{ker}(h)\rightarrow \sigma^{\operatorname{gp}}/\mathbb Zu_v.$$

Let $D_{v,\sigma}\subset X_\sigma$ be the toric divisor associated to $\rho_v$. The restriction of $ \underline{\overline Y_v}$ to the Zariski open $a^\ast \sigma$ of $a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})$ is $[D_{v,\sigma}/X^\circ_\sigma]$. 
Its map to $a^\ast\rho=[\mathbb A^1/\mathbb G_m]$ factors through the inclusion of the closed point $B\mathbb G_m$, and thus there is an isomorphism
$$
U_\sigma = [D_{v,\sigma}/X_\sigma^\circ]\times_{B\mathbb G_m}\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb C
\cong [D_{v,\sigma}/T_{\ker(h)}].
$$
But $D_{v,\sigma}$ is an affine toric variety whose dense torus we denote $D_{v,\sigma}^\circ$. By definition of star, $V_\sigma$ is $[D_{v,\sigma}/D_{v,\sigma}^\circ]$. The lattice isomorphism $g$ now provides the second isomorphism in the identification:
$$ V_\sigma \cong  [D_{v,\sigma}/D_{v,\sigma}^\circ] \cong [D_{v,\sigma}/T_{\ker(h)}]\cong U_\sigma.$$
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
Under $\iota$ the morphism (which we think of as the universal expansion) 
    $$\pi_1\colon \underline{A_0\times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}} a^\ast(\mathpzc{Z}_{K}({\mathpzc{A}})\times_{\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(\mathpzc{A})}\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A}))}\rightarrow \underline{\Delta_0\times_{a^\ast \rho} a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})}$$ pulls back to 
    $$\pi_2\colon \underline{A_0 \times_{a^\ast \mathpzc{A}}a^\ast(\mathpzc{Z}_{\mathbf{n}(v)}\times_{\operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)}\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s))}\rightarrow \underline{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)}$$ by Lemma \ref{lem:UnivOverComponent}. 
    
    In particular $\operatorname{Hilb}^{[n+1]}(\pi_1)$ pulls back to $\operatorname{Hilb}^{[n+1]}(\pi_2)$ along $\iota$. Moreover, tracking the Hilbert polynomial of the subscheme in each stratum shows that the locally closed subset $A^{[n+1]}_\Lambda\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times_{a^\ast \rho} \Delta} \underline{Y_v}$ of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{[n+1]}(\pi_1)$ where a stratum associated to a cone $\kappa$ of weight $w(\kappa) = n_i$ contains a length $n_i$ subscheme (cf. Theorem~\ref{thm:LogHilbProper}) pulls back to an open subset of $\operatorname{Hilb}^{[n+1]}(\pi_2)$ isomorphic to
    $$(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[\textbf{n}(v)]}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}:=\left(\prod_i(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[n_i]}\right)\times_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)}a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$$ 
    (cf. Theorem~\ref{thm:ComponentlogHilb}). 
    
    We have thus specified a morphism of algebraic stacks $$t\colon \underline{(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[\textbf{n}(v)]}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}} \longrightarrow \underline{{A^{[n+1]}\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times_{^\ast \rho} \Delta} E}}.$$
    To complete the proof we let $$(A^{\circ})^{(\textbf{n}(v))}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}:=\left(\prod_i(A^\circ)^{(n_i)}\right)\times_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)}a^\ast\operatorname{Kum}^\Gamma_{\textbf{n}(v)}(\mathbb{Z}^s)$$
    and write 
    $$t^\circ \colon \underline{(A^{\circ})^{(\textbf{n}(v))}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}} \longrightarrow \underline{{A^{(n+1)}\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times_{^\ast \rho} \Delta} E}}$$ for the restriction of $t$ to the locus of subschemes with support inside $A^\circ$. The morphism $t^\circ$ is obtained by pushing forward under $k$ different open immersions $\underline{A^\circ}\hookrightarrow A$. Each inclusion is $A^\circ$ equivariant and thus determined by the image of the identity in $A^\circ$. Write $m_1,...,m_k$ for the image of the identity under each of these maps. Note that the image of $\sum_j n_j m_j$ in $A/A^\circ$ is zero, and thus $\sum_j n_j m_j$ lies in $A^\circ$. Indeed, this was achieved by taking a fibre product with $a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma$. Applying an automorphism to the first copy of $A^\circ$ - i.e. modifying $m_1$ by post-multiplying by some element of $A^\circ$ and noting that $A^\circ$ is divisible- we may assume that $\sum_j n_j m_j$ is the identity.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                           
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       

    Consider the following commutative square in the category of schemes
    $$\begin{tikzcd}
{\underline{(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[\textbf{n}(v)]}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}}} \arrow[r, "t"] \arrow[d,"HC"] \arrow[dd, "m"', bend right=60] & {\underline{A^{[n+1]}\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times_{^\ast \rho} \Delta} E}} \arrow[d, "HC"] \arrow[dd, "S", bend left=90, looseness=1.8] \\
\underline{(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{(\textbf{n}(v))}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}} \arrow[r,"t'"] \arrow[d, "m'", dashed] & {\underline{A^{(n)}\times_{\mathpzc{A}^{[n+1]}\times_{^\ast \rho} \Delta} E}} \arrow[d, "S'", dashed] \\
\underline{A^\circ} \arrow[r] & \underline{A^\circ}
\end{tikzcd}$$
The morphism $t'$ is defined similarly to $t$ but on the level of Chow variety of points.
The morphisms labelled $HC$ are Hilbert--Chow morphisms, and the top square commutes because the Hilbert--Chow map commutes with open immersion. The morphism $m'$ (resp. $S'$) is multiplication in the group law of $A^{\operatorname{log}}$ (resp. $A$) (weighted where a point appears multiple times in the symmetric product). 

The proof of (2) will be complete if we identify the fibres of $S\circ t$ and $m$ over the identity, and thus follows once we know that $S \circ t = m$. This is immediate from our last paragraph once we check that $S'\circ t' = m'$. 
Since $(A^{\operatorname{log}})^{[\textbf{n}_i]}_{a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_\Gamma}$ is irreducible and $A^\circ$ is separated, by \cite[Tag~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01RH}{01RH}]{stacks} it will suffice to show that these maps agree on the (scheme theoretically dense in any model) open $\prod_i(A^{\circ})^{[n_i]}$. 
But we observed that the restriction $t^\circ$ of $t'$ is pushforward under $k$ inclusions, and thus this last claim follows from elementary group theory once we recall that $\sum_j n_j m_j$ is the identity.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{corr:DualIntCx}
    The dual intersection complex of $\mathcal{X}_0$ is canonically $B_\Lambda$.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
Certainly we have a morphism $$\mathcal{X}_0\rightarrow a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\times_{a^\ast\rho}\Delta_0$$ and points of $a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\times_{a^\ast\rho}\Delta_0$ are in canonical, specialisation preserving, bijection with strata of $B_\Lambda$. Moreover, Theorem \ref{prop:ExplicitDescription} identifies the stratum associated to each point of $a^\ast \operatorname{Kum}_{2n}^\Lambda(\mathpzc{A})\times_{a^\ast\rho}\Delta_0$ with a logarithmic stratum of $\operatorname{Kum}^{\Gamma}_{\textbf{n}(v)}(A^{\operatorname{log}})$ for some choice of $\Gamma$. But each of these logarithmic strata is irreducible by Proposition~\ref{prop:KummerStrataIrreducible}(3) and the claim is proved.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- proposition-15: body_md -->
\label{prop:HodgeTheoryRecall}
    Let $A$ be a conventional abelian surface over $\mathbb{C}$, and let $n\geq 2$ be an integer. There is an isomorphism of Hodge structures, $$H^2(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\mathbb{Z})\cong H^2(A,\mathbb{Z})\oplus \langle \delta \rangle$$
    and using $q$ to define a bilinear form on the right hand side, $\delta$ is a class such that $q(\delta,\delta)=-2(n+1)$ and $q(\delta,x)=0$ whenever $x\in H^2(A,\mathbb{Z})$. Moreover, under this isomorphism $2\delta$ is identified with the class of the exceptional divisor of the Hilbert--Chow morphism restricted to the Kummer variety. Finally $\delta$ has Hodge type $(1,1)$.
<!-- end proposition-15 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
\label{rem:MoveClasses}
    We pause to explain a canonical inclusion $$\hat{\iota}\colon H^2(A,\mathbb{Z})\hookrightarrow H^2(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\mathbb{Z}).$$
    Write $\operatorname{p}_i\colon A^{n+1}\rightarrow A$ for the $i^\text{th}$ projection map, and note that given a class $\eta$ in $H^2(A,\mathbb{Z})$ the form $\eta^{n+1} = \sum_i \operatorname{p}_i^\ast \eta$ descends to a form $\eta^{(n+1)}$ on the symmetric product $A^{(n+1)}$. Pullback of $\eta^{(n+1)}$ along the Hilbert--Chow map defines a class $\eta^{[n+1]}$ on $A^{[n+1]}$. Let $\hat{\iota}(\eta)$ be the restriction of $\eta^{[n+1]}$ to the generalised Kummer variety.
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- definition-50: body_md -->
\label{defn:PrincipalPolarisation}
    Let $(X,L)$ be a polarised IHS variety of generalised Kummer type. We say that the polarisation $L$ is \textit{principal} if there exists an integer $N$ and a choice of lattice isometry $$H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \cong U\oplus U \oplus U \oplus \langle \delta \rangle$$ which identifies $L$ with a class of the form $NH -\delta$ where $H\in U^{\oplus 3}$ and $q_{U^{\oplus 3}}(H,H) = 2$.
<!-- end definition-50 -->
<!-- definition-51: body_md -->
\label{defn:K2nH}
    Fix a positive integer $N$. We define the Noether--Lefschetz locus $\operatorname{NL}(N)$ to be the locus in the moduli of principally polarised IHS varieties $(X,L)$ of generalised Kummer type such that $q(L,L) = 2N^2-2(n+1)$ and also there exists a class $\delta\in H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ which satisfies the following hypotheses.
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item The class $\delta$ is of Hodge type $(1,1)$.
        \item There is an equality $q(\delta,\delta) = -2(n+1)$.
        \item The image $q(\delta,-) = \delta^\vee$ of $\delta$ in $\Lambda^\vee$ has divisibility $2(n+1)$ in $\Lambda^\vee$.                                                                      
        \item There is an equality $q(\delta,L) = 2(n+1)$.
        \item The class $L+\delta$ is $N$ times a primitive class.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-51 -->
<!-- remark-19: body_md -->
In the sequel we would like to argue that the Hodge structure on $H^2(A,\mathbb{Z})$ can be recovered from the principal polarisation class together with the Hodge structure on $H^2(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\mathbb{Z})$. This is a key tool for relating the generalised Kummer locus to the moduli of principally polarised abelian varieties. Fortunately by Eichler's criterion, see \cite[Proposition~3.3]{GritsenkoHulekSankaran}, for any choice of $\delta$ satisfying the hypotheses of Definition \ref{defn:K2nH} there is a lattice isometry such that $$H^2(X,\mathbb{Z}) \cong U\oplus U \oplus U \oplus \langle {\delta} \rangle.$$
    However, whilst the first three summands are determined by a choice of $\delta$ (as its orthogonal complement under $q$), one can worry that there are many choices of $\delta$ satisfying our hypotheses, at least for small values of $N$. Later we will fix $N$ large and argue that this makes $\delta$ unique.
<!-- end remark-19 -->
<!-- proposition-16: body_md -->
\label{prop:TangentSpaceANDUniquePointwise}
    We establish the following facts. 
    \begin{enumerate}[leftmargin = *]
        \item Let $x\in \operatorname{NL}(N)$ be a point associated to a polarised IHS variety $(X,L=NH-\delta)$ such that there exists a unique class $\delta$ in $H^2(X,\mathbb{Z})$ satisfying the hypotheses listed in Definition \ref{defn:K2nH}. The period map identifies the Zariski tangent space $T_x\operatorname{NL}(N)$ with $\langle H,\delta\rangle^\perp\cap H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{C})$.
        \item Let $A$ be any abelian surface and $H$ any principal polarisation for $A$ (i.e. $q(H,H)=2$). Let $\delta$ be half of the Hilbert--Chow exceptional class in $H^2(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A),\mathbb{Z})$. There is an integer $N_0$, which does not depend on $A$, such that for all $N>N_0$, the class $\delta$ in the cohomology of the principally polarised generalised Kummer variety $(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A), NH -\delta)$ is the unique class satisfying the hypotheses of Definition \ref{defn:K2nH}. 
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end proposition-16 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
For claim (1) note the tangent space to the moduli of IHS manifolds is canonically $H^1(X,T_X)$, and the symplectic form induces an isomorphism  $ H^1(X,T_X) \cong H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{C})$. The locus $\operatorname{NL}(N)$ consists of varieties with a polarisation and satisfying five conditions. Conditions (2-5) are open and thus \'etale locally $\operatorname{NL}(N)\subset M_\text{IHS}$ is the closed subset characterised by the existence of a polarisation $L$ and class $\delta$ described in condition (1). By \cite[Lemma 5.16]{Voisin_2003}, the tangent space to the Noether--Lefschetz locus associated to $\delta$ is $\langle \delta \rangle^\perp\subset H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{C})$. Similarly the tangent space of the NL divisor associated to $H$ is $\langle H \rangle^\perp\subset H^{1,1}(X,\mathbb{C})$. Since $\delta$ is not ample but $L$ is, the sublattice $\langle H,\delta \rangle$ which contains $L$ has rank $2$ and so these Noether--Lefschetz loci intersect transversely, and their intersection has tangent space as described in (1).

    We now prove (2). By \cite[Section 1.10]{Huybrechts1999} the restriction of $q$ to the N\'eron--Severi group $\operatorname{NS}_\mathbb{R} = \mathbb{R}\otimes \operatorname{NS}(\operatorname{Kum}_{2n}(A))$ has signature $(1,\rho-1)$ for $\rho$ the Picard rank. We know that $q(H,H)=2>0$, and thus the restriction of $q$ to the orthogonal complement $H^\perp$ of $H$ is negative definite.

    Take any $\delta'$ in $\operatorname{NS}(X)$ which satisfies the hypotheses of Definition \ref{defn:K2nH}. Note that there is a unique way to express $\delta' = aH + y$ in $\operatorname{NS}_\mathbb{R}$ where $y \in H^\perp$ and $a = q(\delta',H)/q(H,H)\in (1/2)\mathbb{Z}$. Constraints (2) and (4) of Definition \ref{defn:K2nH} are now 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:constr} q(\delta',\delta')= 2a^2 + q(y,y) = -2(n+1)\quad \quad q(\delta',L)  = 2Na - q(y,\delta) = 2(n+1).\end{equation}

    Both $y$ and $\delta$ lie in $H^\perp$ where $-q$ is positive definite, so we may apply Cauchy--Schwarz to $-q$ with inputs $y,\delta$.
